confirmed.title: Subscriptions and credits buy nothing on the web: SPA never meters, never tier-gates, and has no API-key UI
confirmed.claim: A Pro/Student subscriber or pack buyer receives no usable entitlement: browser searches are unmetered and un-tiered, and the only metered surface (/api/search via API key) has no customer path to a key.
confirmed.evidence: src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx:58-59 `deduct` is a no-op ('spend goes through the server'); grep 'api/search' in src/ (excluding adapters) matches ONLY src/components/admin/GoldSetHarness.jsx:52,97 — the public search hook never calls the metered endpoint; grep 'tier|allowedSourceIds|CORE_SOURCE_IDS' in src/ finds no gating (App.jsx:61 uses tier only for the PricingPanel 'Current' badge); api/_shared/plans.js:8 says tier restricts 'which sources it may search' but that is enforced only in api/search.js:205; keys minting exists only server-side (api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:50-67) with no client caller.
confirmed.impact: Any Stripe charge is disputable as 'paid for nothing': the customer sees identical search behaviour before and after paying. Pricing copy 'All 22 databases' / '1,000 searches every month' (src/constants/pricing.js:41-45,57-61) describes an entitlement the product does not deliver on the web.
confirmed.fix_hint: Decide the product contract before charging: either (a) route browser searches through /api/search with session auth and tier/credit enforcement, or (b) ship the API-key management UI and re-word plans as API entitlements. Do not enable Stripe prices until one is done.

votes.corrected_claim: Subscriptions and packs deliver no web entitlement. Browser searches never touch the metered endpoint: src/hooks/useSearch.js:46-70 fans out via runSearch(adapter, ...) straight to upstreams (or to the unauthenticated, unmetered same-origin shims api/search/[source].js and the gallica/opencontext/openedition edge routes, whose only guard is requireInternalOrigin); BillingContext.deduct is a no-op (BillingContext.jsx:58-59) and the "future billing hook" in src/adapters/_shared/base.js:6-13 was never wired. The only tier enforcement is allowedSourceIds() in api/search.js:205 (API-key path). The SourcesPanel (Panels.jsx:106-160) gates only on needsKey, never on plan, so an ANONYMOUS web user already gets the full "all" tier — including the backend-keyed DPLA/Europeana/Smithsonian sources that plans.js reserves for paid tiers — i.e. the web over-delivers the paid tier to everyone, while the Plans panel promises "Upgrade for more monthly searches and the full source library" (Panels.jsx:220) and "All 22 databases / 1,000 searches every month" (pricing.js:41-45,57-61). A subscriber (plan=pro, the HUMAN rail per plans.js:13) would only be entitled on /api/search, which has no customer key path (no client calls POST /api/keys; keys.js:50-67 is server-only).
votes.reasoning:
LENS 1 (refutation, all read-only): Every cited anchor checks out. BillingContext.jsx:58-59 `const deduct = useCallback(() => Promise.resolve(true), [])` with the comment "No-op for now — spend goes through the server". `grep -rn "api/search" src | grep -v src/adapters` returns only GoldSetHarness.jsx:52,97 (admin). useSearch.js has zero fetch/apiCall lines; it imports ADAPTERS/runSearch (line 2) and calls runSearch per adapter (lines 63,70,116) — pure client-side fan-out. Adapters that do hit /api/search/<slug> (dpla/europeana/smithsonian → api/search/[source].js; gallica/opencontext/openedition edge) go through routes whose only guard is requireInternalOrigin (F-407) — no session, no plan, no meter. `grep -rnE "tier|allowedSourceIds|CORE_SOURCE_IDS" src` (non-adapter) hits only BillingContext state plumbing and App.jsx:61/304 feeding PricingPanel currentPlan. plans.js:8 says tier = "which sources it may search"; the only consumer is api/search.js:205 `allowedSourceIds(identity.plan, [...SERVER_SAFE_IDS])`. `grep -rn "api/keys" src` is empty; keys.js:49-67 POST mints with plan=DEFAULT_PLAN_ID. pricing.js:41-45,57-61 copy confirmed verbatim. I tried to refute via "web is free by design, subs are API-only": refuted by plans.js:13 ("HUMANS subscribe"), pricing.js:11 (subscriptions sold via web/desktop Stripe AND native IAP — an IAP entitlement can only be the app itself), and Panels.jsx:220 web copy promising more searches + full library. Also checked the webhook (webhook.js:139-151): pack purchase only increments total_credits, never sets plan=machine — consistent with established facts. Fact holds; I only sharpened it (anonymous web users already receive the paid "all" tier, including backend-keyed Wave-3 sources, via unauthenticated shims).

LENS 2 (impact): Not moot. Restoring Supabase re-enables sign-in/checkout but does not create an entitlement — a Pro subscriber post-restore would still see identical web behaviour, and packs still grant credits spendable only through an API key nobody can obtain. For "MVP + first revenue in ~30 days" this is the gating product-contract decision: charging a card before either (a) session-authed metered web search with tier gating or (b) a key-management UI + API-worded plans invites disputes and is arguably a consumer-protection problem. Zero traffic lowers present loss but not the blocker status; option (b) is ~1-2 days of work and must precede enabling Stripe prices. P0 stands (it is the precondition for any revenue at all).

LENS 3 (novelty): The ESTABLISHED FACTS already cover the API-key half (no client POST /api/keys, plan=machine never assigned, Student unpurchasable). What is NEW here and untracked anywhere: (1) the web/browser surface — the HUMAN subscription rail — is entirely unmetered and un-tier-gated (deduct no-op, useSearch bypasses /api/search, SourcesPanel gates only on needsKey), so subscriptions buy nothing on the web even after DB restore; (2) anonymous users already receive the paid "all" tier for free via the unauthenticated [source].js/edge shims; (3) pricing/Plans copy describes an undelivered entitlement. Searched findings.json (no hits for unmetered/entitlement/key UI beyond F-413 key cap), sprint_log_v0_44.md (no meter/tier/key entries), sprint_log_v0_45.md (T9 only fixes non-stacking allowance copy; D-4 drops ApiKey.plan; nothing on web metering or key UI), memory project_v0_30 ("one wire-up left: credit SPEND in search.js" — done for the API in v0.32, browser never addressed). The only trace is the unfulfilled comment at src/adapters/_shared/base.js:13 ("will call BillingContext.deduct() here"), which is a TODO, not a tracked finding. Not fixed in tree. adds_new = true. Overall holds = true.

confirmed.title: No self-serve path to an API key or developer docs; pack buyers pay $10–$200 and receive nothing usable (plan stays 'free', core-only)
confirmed.claim: The Plans panel sells credit packs 'Bought on the web dashboard' but no dashboard, key-management UI, or docs page exists; the only mint route (POST /api/keys) has zero client callers, mints plan=free, and the Stripe webhook never upgrades a pack buyer to the 'machine' tier.
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "api/keys\|/keys" src` → 0 hits. api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:8 documents POST mint, :60 `const planId = DEFAULT_PLAN_ID` (free → api/_shared/plans.js:33 tier 'core', :36 30 req/min). api/stripe/webhook.js:139 only `total_credits: { increment }` for packs; `grep -n machine api/stripe/webhook.js` → no assignment. src/components/Panels.jsx:265-267 "For developers & AI agents … Bought on the web dashboard." Live: `curl https://citation.today/docs` → 200 SPA shell (1849B), `/api/openapi.json` → 404, `/api/docs` → 404. Footer (src/components/Layout.jsx:248-256) has no docs/API/GitHub/ToS link. mcp/README.md:85 says the key is "Optional today (free tier is open)" while live `/api/search` returns 401 without a key (established fact) and :94 tells developers to run `npm run print-schemas` from a repo checkout to get the OpenAPI spec. MCP package not on npm (established fact).
confirmed.impact: The paid API is the only product with real gating, and it is unreachable: a developer cannot discover the endpoint, cannot obtain a key, and a pack purchase yields credits on a key-less, core-only free plan. Direct refund/chargeback risk on every pack sale; zero developer/agent acquisition.
confirmed.fix_hint: Ship a 'Developers' panel: list/mint/revoke keys via existing /api/keys (show plaintext once), curl + MCP quickstart, link to a served OpenAPI JSON (mcp/src/schema.js already generates one — expose via an Edge route, free under the 12-function cap). In the webhook, set User.plan='machine' (or mint keys with the user's plan) on checkout.session.completed for packs. Fix mcp/README:85 and publish the MCP package or document local install honestly.

votes.corrected_claim: No paid SKU yields a usable entitlement. Credits from packs AND subscriptions land only on User.total_credits, which is spendable solely via /api/search with an x-api-key; the web app never meters (useSearch/src/lib have zero /api/search or x-api-key callers) and gates no feature on plan (grep for plan/isPro/premium in src → 0 hits). The only mint route (POST /api/keys, api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:8) has zero client callers, its comment at :58-59 promises a 'credit purchase flow' that assigns a paid plan, but api/stripe/webhook.js:137-150 only increments total_credits for packs and sets User.plan only for `subscription: true` plans — so a pack buyer stays plan=free (apiAuth.js:67,82 resolves plan from user.plan; the ApiKey.plan column is ignored). Pack credits are therefore NOT literally lost: a buyer who hand-crafts a session-cookie POST /api/keys could spend them at core tier / 30 req/min — but there is no self-serve UI, no docs (/docs, /openapi.json, /llms.txt all return the 1849B SPA catch-all shell; /api/openapi.json and /api/docs → 404), no footer link (Layout.jsx:247-255), Panels.jsx:267 promises a 'web dashboard' that does not exist, and mcp/README.md:85 falsely says the key is optional while live /api/search returns 401.
votes.reasoning:
LENS 1 (factual): Every citation checked out read-only. `grep -rn "api/keys\|/keys" src` → 0 hits. keys.js:60 `const planId = DEFAULT_PLAN_ID` (plans.js:90 = "free"; free = tier core, 30/min at plans.js:33-40). webhook.js:139 pack path only `total_credits: { increment }`; :141-150 plan assignment guarded by `getPlan(planId).subscription` and checkout.js:72 sends `metadata = { pack }` with no plan, so 'machine' (plans.js:62-70, payg, never referenced in webhook — grep confirmed) is unreachable. Panels.jsx:265-267 copy verified. Footer verified (no links). Live: /docs 200/1849B, /api/openapi.json 404, /api/docs 404, /api/keys 401; also /openapi.json, /llms.txt, /.well-known/mcp.json all 200/1849B — i.e. SPA catch-all, so the '/docs → 200' evidence is a trivial artifact of the rewrite, not a doc page (minor overstatement). mcp/README.md:85 and :94 verified. One correction: 'receive nothing usable' is slightly too strong — credits are spendable via a hand-minted key at core tier; the corrected claim above captures that. Added finding from verification: subscriptions (Pro/Student) have the same dead-end because the web app neither meters nor plan-gates anything, so the defect covers every SKU, not just packs.
LENS 2 (impact): Even after Supabase is restored (prerequisite P0), the first honest dollar requires a buyer to get something for it; today every SKU delivers credits the buyer cannot reach without reverse-engineering POST /api/keys. That is a refund/chargeback and reputational liability on sale #1 and blocks any developer/agent acquisition (no docs, no served spec, MCP unpublished). Zero traffic means no damage yet, but the 30-day goal is first revenue, and this sits squarely on that critical path — P0 stands. Fix is small and within constraints: a Developers panel over existing GET/POST/DELETE /api/keys, webhook `plan: 'machine'` on pack checkout (or derive tier from purchases), and an Edge route serving the OpenAPI JSON that mcp/src/schema.js already generates (Edge is exempt from the 12-function cap).
LENS 3 (novelty): The ESTABLISHED FACTS already state 'no customer path to an API key', 'plan=machine never assigned', 'pack buyer stays plan=free'. This finding adds depth beyond that: (a) Panels.jsx:267 ships a false 'web dashboard' promise; (b) keys.js:58-59 documents a purchase→plan flow that was never built; (c) no docs/spec surface at all and mcp/README:85 contradicts live 401 behaviour; (d) the web app gates nothing on plan and never meters, so subscriptions are equally unusable (broader than established facts); (e) concrete fix path. Not fixed in the working tree (v0.44 touches none of keys/webhook/Panels copy). Not tracked: docs/wiki/_machine/findings.json and _fragments have no entry for missing key UI, machine assignment, or docs (only F-413 key-count cap and the webhook-metadata-trust finding); sprint_log_v0_45.md covers ledger/webhook races, not plan assignment or key UI; sprint_log_v0_44.md is engine teardown. The archived sprint_log_v0_37 (docs/wiki-gh/99-Archive, status PLAN READY, never executed) proposed a key-generation UI via a different route (/api/keys/generate + connect-ai) but does not cover the webhook machine-plan gap or served docs. Verdict: holds.

confirmed.title: Supabase OpenC_Auth paused ~10 weeks on Free plan with zero backups and no off-site dump — all user/key/credit data is one policy tick from unrecoverable
confirmed.claim: The only persistent copy of users, accounts, sessions, api_keys, api_usage, processed_events, search_history, library_items and relevance_labels is a Free-plan Supabase project that is INACTIVE; the Free plan takes no daily backups and the repo contains no dump/backup tooling, so the pause-time logical backup Supabase holds is the sole copy.
confirmed.evidence: Supabase MCP get_project cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq → status "INACTIVE", db host db.cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq.supabase.co, created 2026-05-10; get_organization wxyjeuyqxeweeqgmxobf → plan "free". Last proof DB was alive: Vercel build log of prod deploy dpl_2ZTVC6KJHiFH9NKFBvdHni3q82P3 (2026-06-10 07:08 UTC) "Datasource … aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432 … 3 migrations found … No pending migrations to apply". Supabase docs (free-project-pausing): pause after ~7 days of low DB activity; restore via dashboard "up to 1 year after it was paused"; changelog 27497 (June 2024) previously set the window at 90 days and third-party 2026 guides still cite 90 days. Supabase backups doc: Free plan has no automated backups ("regularly export … db dump"); PITR requires Pro + Small compute. `grep -rln "pg_dump|db dump|supabase db"` over the repo → no matches. Runtime error 2026-09-01 "FATAL: Tenant or user not found" from the pooler is Supavisor de-registering the paused tenant (github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/30107, /35749) — consistent with pause, NOT deletion (project still listed, db host still assigned). Estimated pause date: 2026-06-17..24 (7-day inactivity after the last known activity on 06-10) → ~70-77 days paused on 2026-09-02; under the older 90-day rule one-click restore would close ~2026-09-15..22, under the current 1-year rule ~June 2027. Confidence on pause date is inference.
confirmed.impact: If the 90-day interpretation is the one enforced (or the 1-year window lapses unnoticed, which is how the last 10 weeks went), the only recovery is downloading the pause-time .backup and rebuilding a new project by hand; if Supabase deletes the project, every registered user, every issued oc_live_ key hash, every credit balance and every Stripe processed_events row is gone permanently. Until restore, sign-in, credits, history, library, settings sync, API-key auth, checkout and the Stripe webhook are all dead (verified by the orchestrator's 09-01 PrismaClientInitializationError).
confirmed.fix_hint: Order of operations for Shahbaz: (1) Supabase dashboard → OpenC_Auth → "Resume project" (or MCP restore_project); wait for ACTIVE_HEALTHY. (2) Verify with MCP list_tables / execute_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM users, api_keys, processed_events, library_items, search_history, _prisma_migrations (expect the 3 migration rows). (3) IMMEDIATELY take an off-site dump: `supabase db dump --db-url <session-pooler url> -f opencite-$(date +%F).sql` and store it outside Vercel/Supabase; add this to a weekly routine. (4) Prevent re-pause: either upgrade the org to Pro ($25/mo: no pausing + 7-day daily backups) or add a keepalive (a daily Vercel cron hitting a tiny Prisma query — Hobby allows daily crons — is enough per Supabase's "a few requests a day" threshold). What restore does NOT recover: nothing DB-side is lost within the window, but every `sessions` row will be expired (all users re-login), the pooler tenant may need a password reset if "Tenant or user not found" persists after resume, and if you end up on the new-project path the project ref changes → POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL/POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING in Vercel and the ops_credentials memory must be rewritten.

votes.corrected_claim: The only persistent copy of users/accounts/sessions/api_keys/api_usage/processed_events/search_history/library_items/relevance_labels is Free-plan Supabase project OpenC_Auth (cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq), currently INACTIVE; Free plan has no automated backups and the repo/CI contain no dump tooling, so the pause-time backup is the sole copy. CORRECTION to the window: Supabase's current docs (free-project-pausing and platform/upgrading, "Time limits") state one-click restore is available for 90 DAYS after pause (rule in force since 2024-06-24) — there is no "up to 1 year" rule. After 90 days the project drops to download-.backup-and-rebuild-a-new-project only. With last known DB activity 2026-06-10 and Supabase's ~7-day inactivity + ~1-week warning cadence (and a third project 'launchpad' created in the same free org on 2026-06-22, consistent with OpenC_Auth already being paused by then), the one-click window most likely closes ~2026-09-15..22, i.e. roughly 11-18 days from today (2026-09-04).
votes.reasoning: LENS 1 (refutation): Tried to falsify and could not. prisma/schema.prisma:10-13 is the only datasource (POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL / POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING), so all Prisma models live in that one Postgres. Supabase MCP get_project cjnmoupvlqcqigmabanq -> status INACTIVE, created 2026-05-10, PG 17.6.1.121; get_organization wxyjeuyqxeweeqgmxobf -> plan "free". list_projects shows all three org projects INACTIVE and no sibling copy of the DB. Repo grep (case-insensitive pg_dump|db dump|supabase db|backup|PITR, excluding node_modules) hits only the F-404 finding text and an OpenEdition dossier table row — no tooling; package.json scripts = dev/build/migrate only; vercel.json has no crons; no .github/workflows; scripts/ = migrate.mjs, admin/stress probes, wiki builder. Supabase backups doc: automated daily backups are Pro/Team/Enterprise only; Free is told to export via `supabase db dump`. The one place the finding is WRONG is the restore window: it claims the current rule is "up to 1 year" with 90 days as the older rule. Supabase's current docs say the opposite — free-project-pausing: "You can restore a paused project for up to 90 days after it was paused"; platform/upgrading "Time limits": "Starting from 2024-06-24 ... 90-day window ... After the 90-day restore window, you can download your project's backup file" and rebuild in a new project. So the corrected claim is strictly more urgent. Pause date remains inference (no API field exposes it; Vercel runtime-error lookback is capped at 7d), but the org's third project was created 2026-06-22, which on a free org (2 active projects max) is consistent with OpenC_Auth having been auto-paused by then. LENS 2 (impact): Not moot. Every revenue path (sign-in, API-key auth, credits, Stripe webhook idempotency via processed_events, checkout) requires this DB; v0.44/v0.45 do not touch infrastructure and cannot ship a working money path without it. Zero traffic means the data volume is small, but it includes the admin user, any issued oc_live_ key hashes, and the Stripe processed_events ledger — recreating from scratch is possible but the 90-day cliff converts a 1-click restore into a manual .backup import and a project-ref/env-var rewrite, and the same inattention that let it pause for ~11 weeks is exactly what will let the window lapse. Cost of the fix is minutes (Resume + `supabase db dump`). P0 stands: it is the single hard blocker on MVP + first revenue and has a hard deadline inside the 30-day horizon. LENS 3 (novelty): The ESTABLISHED FACTS and memory project_prod_state_2026_09.md record only that the project is paused and auth/billing are dead. Nothing in docs/wiki/_machine/findings.json (F-500..F-509 are env-var names, migrations, FK, billing audit, pins, MCP, localStorage keys, output.css), sprint_log_v0_44.md (no supabase/postgres mention), or sprint_log_v0_45.md (mentions Supabase only for branch-testing migrations) tracks the no-backup/no-dump exposure, the 90-day restore cliff, or a re-pause prevention (keepalive/Pro). The added depth — sole-copy status, absent tooling, Free-plan no-backup policy, and a dated deadline — is new and actionable. Verdict: holds, with the restore-window claim corrected from "1 year (current) / 90 days (old)" to "90 days (current)".

confirmed.title: Webhook reads pre-basil `line.price.id`; on a 2025-03-31+ API version the first-invoice grant can resolve to the FREE allowance
confirmed.claim: priceIdFromInvoice depends on `lines.data[].price` / `.plan`, both removed from Invoice Line Items in Stripe API 2025-03-31.basil; on such a webhook version planIdForPriceId returns null and the code falls back to User.plan, which is still 'free' if invoice.paid arrives before checkout.session.completed.
confirmed.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:41-44 reads `l.price.id || l.plan.id`; :160-164 fallback `planId = u?.plan || 'free'`; :165-167 grants monthlyGrantFor('free')=20 and stamps credits_period; :141-150 checkout branch later sets plan 'pro' but grants nothing. node_modules/stripe/cjs/apiVersion.js:5 pins '2025-02-24.acacia' for outbound REQUESTS only — webhook payload shape follows the endpoint/account API version (Stripe changelog 'invoice-pricing-configurations': `price` and `plan` fields are no longer available on Invoice Line Items; replace with `pricing.price_details.price`). Account/endpoint API version NOT verifiable from here (inference).
confirmed.impact: If the Stripe account was created after March 2025 (likely for a project that started May 2026) the very first Pro invoice grants 20 credits instead of 1000 and the month is locked; subsequent renewals then grant the correct plan only because User.plan has been set by then.
confirmed.fix_hint: Read `line.pricing?.price_details?.price` first, then `line.price?.id`; pin the webhook endpoint API version in the Stripe dashboard and record it in webhook.js; add `line.parent?.subscription_item_details` handling if needed.

votes.corrected_claim: On a webhook endpoint whose API version is >= 2025-03-31.basil (the account default for any Stripe account created after that date, unless the endpoint was explicitly pinned), `priceIdFromInvoice` (api/stripe/webhook.js:41-44) always returns null because Invoice Line Items no longer carry `price`/`plan` (replaced by `pricing.price_details.price`). The renewal branch then silently degrades to the User.plan fallback (webhook.js:160-164). Because api/checkout.js:90-98 persists `stripe_customer_id` BEFORE creating the Checkout session, `invoice.paid` for the first invoice resolves the user via `customer` even when it arrives before `checkout.session.completed` — so User.plan is still 'free', `monthlyGrantFor('free')`=20 is applied and `credits_period` is stamped for the month; the later checkout event sets plan='pro' but grants nothing (webhook.js:141-151), and `applyMonthlyGrant` refuses to re-grant that month. Same for Student ($5/500). The Stripe SDK's pinned '2025-02-24.acacia' (node_modules/stripe/cjs/apiVersion.js:5, stripe@17.7.0) governs only outbound requests, not event payload shape. The endpoint/account API version itself is NOT verifiable from the repo — one Dashboard check (Developers > Webhooks > endpoint API version) settles it. Note the invoice already carries the plan via mirrored subscription metadata (checkout.js:107 `subscription_data.metadata.plan`), reachable as `inv.subscription_details.metadata` (acacia) / `inv.parent.subscription_details.metadata` (basil) — a version-agnostic primary signal the webhook never reads.

confirmed.title: OpenAlex metered pricing makes every sold query cost more upstream than it earns
confirmed.claim: Since Feb 2026 OpenAlex bills API usage per call; each /api/search query fires two OpenAlex search calls (OPENALEX + CURATED) at $0.001 each with no server API key, so upstream cost (~$0.002/query) exceeds the $0.00067-$0.001/query pack price and runs on the un-keyed demo budget.
confirmed.evidence: Live: `curl 'https://api.openalex.org/works?search=climate&per-page=1'` and `...?filter=title.search:climate&per-page=1` both return meta `"cost_usd": 0.001`. src/adapters/core/openalex.js:46 and src/adapters/core/curatedJournals.js:42 both call api.openalex.org/works?filter=...search with only `&mailto=` (openalex.js:30-31) — `grep -rn OPENALEX api .env.example` finds no OPENALEX_API_KEY anywhere server-side. Pack prices: src/constants/pricing.js:73-75 ($0.0010/$0.00083/$0.00067 per query). OpenAlex help center: 'A free API key raises your daily budget 10x'; CASRAI summary: ~$1/day free allowance per key, search calls $1.00 per 1,000, un-keyed path 'not suitable for production'.
confirmed.impact: Negative gross margin on the core source alone for every PAYG credit sold; on the un-keyed path the shared prod egress exhausts a small daily demo budget, after which OpenAlex (the largest core source) drops for all customers while credits keep being charged at near-full coverage (OpenAlex failure only lowers the band, it does not zero the charge).
confirmed.fix_hint: Register an OpenAlex API key, inject it server-side (serverKeys.js pattern) and pass `api_key` in openalex.js/curatedJournals.js; collapse the two OpenAlex calls into one per query (CURATED is an OpenAlex filter on ISSNs); re-price packs above ~$0.003/query or cap OpenAlex calls per query; add an upstream-cost line to plans.js so per-source metered cost is visible before enabling a source in the billable set.

votes.corrected_claim: OpenAlex bills search-type calls at $0.001 each (live: meta.cost_usd 0.001 and X-RateLimit-Cost-USD: 0.001 on the exact `filter=is_oa:true,title_and_abstract.search:` shape the adapter sends; list+filter calls are $0.0001, singletons free). Every /api/search query fires TWO such calls (OPENALEX + CURATED, because the server spreads DEFAULT_SETTINGS whose curatedJournals has 4 default ISSNs — defaults.js:13-18,35; search.js:243-247), more for `;`-multi-term queries (search.js:317), with NO server-side key (openAlexKey="" from defaults.js:24; serverKeys.js injects only Europeana/DPLA/Smithsonian; no OPENALEX_API_KEY anywhere). CORRECTIONS: (1) the un-keyed budget is $0.10/day (X-RateLimit-Limit-USD: 0.1 = 1000 credits at 10/search = 100 search calls = ~50 OpenCITE queries/day per egress IP), not ~$1/day; $1/day is the FREE-KEY budget (10x keyless per help.openalex.org). So the marginal-cost problem ($0.002 upstream vs $0.00067-0.001 pack revenue) only bites above ~500 keyed queries/day; the immediate problem is the ~50-query/day un-keyed ceiling shared by ALL API customers on Vercel's egress IP. (2) "OpenAlex failure only lowers the band, it does not zero the charge" is wrong for the tier pack buyers actually land in (plan=free -> core): failed weight 250.01M / total 415.01M -> coverage 0.398 -> band "limited" -> multiplier 0 -> query FREE (coverage.js:36-42,63-69; plans.js freeBelowBand "limited"). On tier `all` it is band "partial" -> 0.5x. BUT after 5 consecutive 429s the circuit breaker (adapterHealth.js FAILURE_STREAK_THRESHOLD=5) drops OPENALEX+CURATED from the eligible set (search.js:237-238) -> failedCount=0 -> band "full" -> 1.0x charge for Crossref+DOAJ-only results until midnight UTC / cold start. Net: once the shared un-keyed budget is spent, customers get a brief free window, then pay FULL price for results missing the largest source. The browser SPA is unaffected (openalex.js:47 fetches api.openalex.org directly from the user's IP; CORS *), though each anonymous web user is capped at ~50 OpenAlex-backed searches/day.
votes.reasoning: LENS 1 (factual): Ran `curl api.openalex.org/works?filter=is_oa:true,title_and_abstract.search:climate&...` (the adapter's exact shape): cost_usd 0.001, headers X-RateLimit-Cost-USD 0.001, X-RateLimit-Limit-USD 0.1, X-RateLimit-Limit 1000, Credits-Used 10, Reset ~11300s. Adding &mailto= does not change cost. list+filter (`filter=is_oa:true`, `filter=cites:`) = 0.0001; singleton = no cost. CASRAI: keys required for production since Feb 2026, search $1/1k, filter $0.10/1k, ~$1/day free per key; help.openalex.org/api-reference/authentication: keyless casual use allowed, "a free key gives you 10x the keyless budget". Code: search.js:243-247 builds settings from {...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...envKeys} so openAlexKey="" and curatedJournals = 4 default ISSNs -> curatedJournals.js:25 does not throw -> both openalex.js:46 and curatedJournals.js:42 fire per query. `grep -rn OPENALEX api .env.example` -> only CORE_SOURCE_IDS and the mailto comment; serverKeys.js has no OpenAlex entry. pricing.js:73-75 / plans.js CREDIT_PACKS confirm $0.0010/$0.00083/$0.00067 per query. Two errors in the finding: un-keyed budget is $0.10/day not ~$1/day; and OpenAlex failure DOES zero the charge on core tier (coverage 0.398 -> "limited" -> 0) — but the v0.38 circuit breaker then removes OPENALEX/CURATED from the denominator after 5 failures, restoring band "full" and 1.0x charge on degraded results, which is worse than claimed. LENS 2 (impact): The margin argument is theoretical at zero traffic and only applies above ~500 keyed queries/day ($1/day free = 1000 search calls); a single pack_10k customer burning 10k queries in a week would cost ~$13-20 upstream vs $10 revenue, so re-pricing/collapsing the double call matters before scale but not for first revenue. What DOES matter for first revenue: with no server key, all API customers combined get ~50 OpenAlex-backed queries/day from Vercel's (shared, possibly multi-tenant) egress IP, after which the breaker silently sells full-price Crossref+DOAJ-only answers. Registering a free key + injecting it via serverKeys.js is a ~30-minute prerequisite to selling any pack. Not moot: DB pause and missing key UI are bigger blockers, but this must ship in the same window. P0 overstated (not a hard blocker, fix is trivial); P1. Also /api/citations is barely affected (singleton free, cites/openalex batch filters $0.0001). LENS 3 (novelty): docs/wiki/02-Adapters/capability-dossiers/openalex.md:198-200 already recorded "$0.001 per list query" and "$1 free credit per day" (with a now-stale anon limit of 10,000/day, X-RateLimit-Limit: 10000 — live un-keyed is 1000 credits/$0.10, so OpenAlex tightened or the probe was keyed), and sprint_log_v0_44.md D-8 explicitly defers the "CURATED/OpenAlex double-call fold-in". Neither connects cost to pack pricing, tracks server-side OPENALEX_API_KEY injection, identifies the un-keyed shared-IP budget, or the breaker->full-charge interaction. Not in findings.json, sprint_log_v0_45.md, or the ESTABLISHED FACTS. adds_new = true. Fix hint stands with one correction: the key alone lifts the ceiling to ~500 queries/day free; collapsing to one OpenAlex call per query halves upstream cost; re-pricing is only needed beyond the free budget.

confirmed.title: No published ToS, privacy, refund or contact surface behind a live Stripe checkout

confirmed.evidence: Footer at src/components/Layout.jsx:248-256 renders only 'Always verify citations...' — no legal links. `curl` https://citation.today/terms, /privacy, /tos, /legal all return the SPA shell (md5 502caecb... identical to /; vercel.json catch-all rewrite line 16-19). Bundle grep for 'terms of service|privacy policy|refund' = 0 hits. docs/wiki/11-Legal/Terms-of-Service.md:11-15 says 'DRAFT ... Do not link it from the live site'; Legal-Overview.md:49-58 lists L2 Privacy, L6, L7 DMCA, L8 footer links as 'not started'. api/checkout.js:101-112 creates the session with no `consent_collection`, no policy URLs; pricing copy shows '$5' with no currency code (src/constants/pricing.js:37,54). Stripe docs 'Website checklist' (docs.stripe.com/get-started/checklist/website) require description, purchase currency, customer-service contact, refund + cancellation policy, privacy policy; 'If your website doesn't include sufficient information about your fulfillment policies, we might request that you add it.'
confirmed.impact: Stripe account review can impose reserves, payout holds or termination; every chargeback on a digital-credit sale is lost by default with no posted refund/cancellation policy (revenue reversal + dispute fees); no contractual limitation of liability or anti-circumvention terms actually bind any paying user because nothing was accepted.
confirmed.fix_hint: Publish ToS + Privacy + Refund/Cancellation + Contact (email, DMCA agent) as static routes (public/legal/*.html or SPA routes excluded from the catch-all), link them in Footer and AuthModal, set `consent_collection: { terms_of_service: 'required' }` and Dashboard 'Public details' policy URLs, show 'USD' next to prices. Counsel review of the draft ToS is the gating item (L1).

confirmed.title: /api/proxy is an unauthenticated, unthrottled bandwidth relay that can exhaust the Hobby transfer cap (site-wide outage)
confirmed.claim: The Edge proxy accepts any GET/POST from anyone, applies no rate limit or size cap, and streams the full upstream body back with ACAO:*; a script can pull multi-hundred-KB responses from 22 allowlisted hosts through Vercel's egress until the Hobby Fast-Data-Transfer quota (100 GB/mo) is hit and Vercel pauses the deployment — taking /api/search, auth and the SPA down with it.
confirmed.evidence: api/proxy.js:57-126 — handler has no auth, no limiter, no Content-Length cap; `return new Response(upstreamRes.body, ...)` (line 123) streams whatever the upstream sends. Live: `curl -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}" "https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=https://www.loc.gov/collections/?fo=json"` → `200 895612 1.185977`. `curl .../api/proxy?url=https://www.loc.gov/robots.txt` → 200 (arbitrary paths). `curl -X POST -d aaaa .../api/proxy?url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/` → 405 (upstream reached; POST bodies relayed, line 111-113). ~112k such requests ≈ 100 GB; one machine can do that in hours. Vercel Hobby also has no per-project WAF/rate-limit enabled (none configured in vercel.json:1-30).
confirmed.impact: Single attacker can knock the entire production deployment offline for the rest of the billing month (Hobby pauses on overage); paid API customers lose availability; additionally the relay lets third parties attack gallica/loc.gov/openlibrary from Vercel IPs, risking IP bans that break those SPA adapters for every user.
confirmed.fix_hint: Gate /api/proxy with requireInternalOrigin-style Sec-Fetch-Site check PLUS a KV/in-memory per-IP limiter; cap streamed bytes (read with a byte budget, e.g. 2 MB, then abort); trim the allowlist to the 8 hosts still called via proxiedFetch (api.dp.la, doi.pangaea.de, dpul.princeton.edu, library.oapen.org, openlibrary.org, ws.pangaea.de, www.lareferencia.info, www.loc.gov); consider Vercel Firewall rate rules.

Live-confirmed 2026-09-04: robots.txt → 200; `openlibrary.org/search.json?q=history&limit=1000&page=3` → 200 / 503,912 B / 8.1 s; `catalogue.bnf.fr/api/SRU…maximumRecords=50` → 200 / 264,696 B; POST to gallica → upstream 405 (relayed). Corrections: (a) the loc.gov `collections/?fo=json` 895 KB probe is NOT reliably reproducible — it now 504s at ~25 s (Edge initial-response timeout), so use the 250–500 KB Open Library / BNF SRU bodies as the abuse unit; (b) exhaustion is FASTER than claimed: Edge-function response bytes are metered as Fast Origin Transfer (Hobby ≈10 GB/mo) as well as Fast Data Transfer (100 GB), so ~20k × 500 KB requests (not ~112k) trips the first Hobby cap; Vercel Hobby docs: after exceeding a limit you "wait until 30 days have passed before you can use the feature again"; (c) Vercel WAF rate limiting IS available on Hobby (1 rule/project, IP or JA4 key, fixed window 10 s–10 min, 1M allowed requests included) — it is not configured in vercel.json because firewall rules are not a vercel.json concern; a single dashboard rule on path /api/proxy is the fastest mitigation; (d) fix-hint allowlist trim to 8 hosts is wrong — the live SPA proxies 11 hosts (also catalogue.bnf.fr, obv-at-oenb.alma.exlibrisgroup.com, api.dc.library.northwestern.edu via bnfApi.js/onb.js/northwestern.js browser branch); trimming to 8 breaks BNF_API/ONB/Northwestern; (e) `requireInternalOrigin` is Node-style (req.headers / res.statusCode) — proxy.js is Edge (Request/Response) so it needs an Edge variant, and Sec-Fetch-Site is only a soft guard against non-browser clients; the byte cap + per-IP limiter are the real controls.

Live (read-only curl against citation.today): robots.txt 200/482 B; POST -d aaaa → gallica 405 with 1,075 B upstream body (relay confirmed); openlibrary limit=1000 page=3 → 200 / 503,912 B / 8.1 s, X-Vercel-Cache MISS; BNF SRU → 200 / 264,696 B; loc.gov collections?fo=json → 504 / 108 B at 25–26 s on two attempts (the finding's 895 KB result is not reproducible; the Edge 25 s initial-response limit caps that particular URL — but it does not cap streaming once headers are sent, and other allowlisted URLs return 250–500 KB fast). Non-allowlisted hosts (data.rijksmuseum.nl, api.base-search.net, api.core.ac.uk, ndl.iitkgp.ac.in) → 403 (allowlist works). Vercel docs fetched: manage-cdn-usage — Fast Origin Transfer = bytes in/out "between the CDN and Vercel Functions" incl. response body, so Edge relay output counts against FOT (Hobby ~10 GB) AND FDT (100 GB); plans/hobby — exceeding a Hobby limit means waiting "until 30 days have passed"; vercel-waf/rate-limiting — Hobby: 1 rate-limit rule/project, IP/JA4 keys, fixed window, 1M allowed requests included (so the fix hint's WAF suggestion is viable and cheap; the finding's implication that Hobby lacks it is wrong). The core claim holds with the corrections above; the quota math is actually worse than stated.

LENS 2 — IMPACT. Against: zero traffic, no attacker incentive today, Supabase paused so money path is dead regardless, and Vercel DDoS mitigation is on by default (but it targets volumetric floods, not a ~5 req/s scraper). For: the endpoint is discoverable from the public SPA bundle (`/api/proxy?url=`), one machine can push ~10 GB of FOT in 1–2 hours (20k × 500 KB at ~8 s each, parallelised), and the consequence on Hobby is not a bill but a 30-day feature pause across the whole project — SPA, /api/search, auth, Stripe checkout — which would erase the entire first-revenue window; POST relay from Vercel egress IPs also risks upstream bans/abuse reports against the account. confirmed.title: Post-checkout return (?checkout=success|cancel) is unhandled: no confirmation, no next step, and the credits chip mislabels pack credits as a monthly allowance
confirmed.claim: Stripe redirects to `/?checkout=success` or `/?checkout=cancel`, but the SPA has zero handling for either param, so a buyer lands on the plain home page with the Plans panel closed, no receipt/next-step, and (for packs) a header chip reading e.g. '10000 left · Remaining searches this month'.
confirmed.evidence: api/checkout.js:110-111 `success_url: \`${base}/?checkout=success\``, `cancel_url: ... ?checkout=cancel`; `grep -rn -i "checkout=success|session_id" src` → 0 hits; live bundle `grep -o checkout=success assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js | wc -l` → 0. src/App.jsx:55 `activePanel` initialises to null (Plans panel not reopened). src/components/Layout.jsx:131-138 CreditsChip renders `{credits} left` with `title="Remaining searches this month"` for any finite balance — a pack buyer on plan=free with 10,000 pack credits sees that label (api/_shared/handlers/credits.js:51-54 returns the raw `total_credits`).
confirmed.impact: Buyers cannot tell whether the purchase worked, are not told how to use what they bought (no key), and the only visible signal is mislabelled; cancel returns silently. High support/refund load per sale.
confirmed.fix_hint: On mount read `checkout` from the URL, open a confirmation panel (success: 'Credits added — create your API key' → keys UI; cancel: reopen Plans), then `history.replaceState` to strip the param. confirmed.title: Round-robin interleave surfaces Crossref's off-topic bibliographic hits at ranks 3/6/9; pass-through thesis fails for the merged list
confirmed.claim: With no ranking layer, the API top-N is result #1 of each adapter in registry order (DOAJ, OPENALEX, CROSSREF, CURATED), so the weakest source's top hit always occupies rank 3; Crossref query.bibliographic ranks on title term overlap and hasContentMatch passes any record matching ONE meaningful term, so for a typical query the interleaved top-9 contains three irrelevant Crossref items and demotes the most-cited relevant OpenAlex paper to rank 5.
confirmed.evidence: Live probe 2026-09-04 (scratchpad/probe.mjs, exact adapter URLs, q='ancient DNA Anatolia'): OPENALEX top-3 = 'Ancient DNA shows domestic horses... Anatolia' (cited 70), 'Genomic insights into the origin of farming in the ancient Near East' (cited 1043), 'Ancient DNA from Mesopotamia... Anatolia' (44); CROSSREF top-3 = 'Personal Names in Ancient Anatolia' (monograph), 'Ancient Landscapes in Southeastern Anatolia' (book), 'The Oxford Handbook of Ancient Anatolia' (none about DNA); DOAJ top-3 = 'Ancient genomes illuminate Eastern Arabian population history...', 'Ancient DNA from European early neolithic farmers...', 'Eastern Mediterranean Mobility... Ancient DNA of Pigs and Cattle'. Registry order src/adapters/index.js:55-58; interleave api/search.js:115-124; Crossref query construction src/adapters/core/crossref.js:38-40 and filter :84 `mapped.filter(r => hasContentMatch(r, words))` where src/adapters/_shared/contentMatch.js:56 is `words.some(...)`. Resulting API order: 1 DOAJ-Arabia, 2 OA-horses, 3 CR-PersonalNames, 4 DOAJ-farmers, 5 OA-farming(1043), 6 CR-Landscapes, 7 DOAJ-pigs, 8 OA-Mesopotamia, 9 CR-Oxford. On the all tier the same slot rule inserts Princeton DPUL Sri Lanka pamphlets (live: 'At the service of the people in Sri Lanka...'), IA-FTS junk title 'f_2171000', and BnF 'Intercultural contacts in the ancient Mediterranean' into the top ~15.
confirmed.impact: A grounding API whose top-10 is ~33% off-topic on a mainstream query; on the all tier precision@25 roughly equals the fraction of sources that are relevant to the query, i.e. heritage/museum noise is guaranteed at fixed ranks. Customers pay full price for it (coverage band is 'full').
confirmed.fix_hint: Cheapest: require all (or >=ceil(n/2)) meaningful terms in hasContentMatch for Crossref, and order interleave lanes by source precision (OpenAlex first) instead of registry order; medium: weight the round-robin by per-source native total/relevance or restore a light RRF over native ranks (rrf.js is in quarantine).

confirmed.title: BASE is IP-denied upstream but counted as covered (30% of the all-tier coverage weight) and is 403 in the browser
confirmed.claim: api.base-search.net requires IP registration; it answers HTTP 200 {"error":"Access denied for IP address ..."} which the adapter parses as data.response undefined -> docs [] -> a successful empty result, so BASE (corpusSize 300M = 30.16% of the serverSafe denominator, larger than OpenAlex) is treated as fully covered on every all-tier query while returning nothing; in the browser proxiedFetch hits /api/proxy which 403s because api.base-search.net is not allowlisted.
confirmed.evidence: Live: probe2 BASE-raw -> HTTP 200 ct=application/json `{"error": "Access denied for IP address 73.118.140.113 and user agent ..."}` for both Chrome and OpenCITE UAs; prod `curl https://citation.today/api/proxy?url=<api.base-search.net...>` -> 403 'Domain api.base-search.net not allowlisted'. Code: base.js:50-55 `const resp = data.response || {}; ... docs = resp.docs || []` (no `.error` check); api/proxy.js:7-30 ALLOWED_DOMAINS lacks api.base-search.net; corpus share computed from the live registry (scratchpad/cov.mjs): BASE 300000000 / 994840000 = 30.16%. Vercel egress IPs are dynamic, so registration is not possible; that the server IP is also denied is inference (0.85).
confirmed.impact: All-tier customers are billed as if a 300M-record aggregator was searched; it never is. Because the adapter does not throw, the v0.38 circuit-breaker never opens and the coverage band never reflects it. If it ever did throw, the band would drop to 'partial' (0.5x) on every query (cov.mjs: 'ALL: BASE fails cov=0.6984 partial').
confirmed.fix_hint: Treat `data.error` as a throw in base.js; either register a static egress IP (Vercel Secure Compute) or drop serverSafe/corpusSize for BASE until it can actually be called; add api.base-search.net to ALLOWED_DOMAINS if browser use is kept.

Whether Vercel's egress IPs are also denied is unverified (no /api/search fan-out in 30 days of prod logs); the 2026-06-09 dossier shows an unregistered residential IP got ~6 successful calls before being blocked, so BASE may intermittently return hits before blocking rather than "never". Correction to the impact chain: if BASE did throw, the band would be `partial` (0.5x) only for the first 5 queries per cold function instance — FAILURE_STREAK_THRESHOLD=5 (adapterHealth.js:24) then drops BASE from eligibility AND the denominator (search.js:238-240), returning the band to `full`. Browser: api.base-search.net has never been in api/proxy.js ALLOWED_DOMAINS (git -S hits were commit-message text only; 403 since v0.29), but BASE is an EXTENSION adapter that is off by default (isAdapterDefaultEnabled = CORE only, src/adapters/index.js:98-99), so only users who toggle it on hit the 403 — which throws "BASE 403" and surfaces as an errored source, not silently. Additionally, BASE's API is non-commercial-only (dossier §10/§14), so even a registered IP would conflict with serving it in the paid `all` tier — favouring the drop-serverSafe/corpusSize remedy over registration.

confirmed.title: scripts/migrate.mjs prints the direct Postgres URL (password included) into Vercel build logs on the fallback path — which the next prod deploy will take while Supabase is paused
confirmed.claim: `run()` logs the full command (`[migrate] $ ${cmd}`, line 34) and the fallback builds `execCmd` with `--url "${DIRECT_URL}"` (lines 59-60), so whenever `prisma migrate deploy` fails in an environment where POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING is set, the connection string with the database password is written verbatim to the build log.
confirmed.evidence: scripts/migrate.mjs:31 `const DIRECT_URL = process.env.POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING || ""`; :34 `console.log(`[migrate] $ ${cmd}`)`; :59-60 `npx prisma db execute --url "${DIRECT_URL}" --file ${sqlFile}`; :47-52 the fallback is entered on ANY `migrate deploy` failure, not just P3005 (comment at :52 says "likely P3005"). Trigger is live today: with the DB paused, `migrate deploy` fails (P1001/tenant-not-found) on the next production build. The preview builds (dpl_DE31…, dpl_94wr…) show the fallback firing on failure — they took the `--schema` branch only because POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING is absent in the Preview env. Vercel build logs are retained per deployment and visible to anyone with project access or a shared inspector link.
confirmed.impact: Database superuser credentials for the only copy of customer/billing data end up in a log store outside the secret manager; anyone who later gets read access to the Vercel project (collaborator, leaked inspector URL, Vercel support) can connect directly, bypassing Prisma, RLS-less tables and the API key hashing. Rotation would then also require touching Vercel env + any dumps.
confirmed.fix_hint: Never interpolate the URL into a logged string: pass it via env (`execSync(cmd, { env: { ...process.env, DATABASE_URL: DIRECT_URL } })` and `--url "$DATABASE_URL"`), or log a redacted copy (`cmd.replace(/:\/\/[^@]+@/, '://***@')`). Also gate the fallback on the actual P3005 error text so an unreachable DB fails fast instead of running four more failing Prisma invocations. If a prod deploy has already happened since the pause, rotate the DB password after restore.

confirmed.title: No monitoring of any kind — the auth/DB outage ran for weeks undetected; Web Analytics unregistered despite <Analytics/> being mounted
confirmed.claim: There is no uptime probe, no error alerting, no analytics registration and only console logging with Hobby-tier retention, so a total loss of sign-in/billing since ~mid-June 2026 produced zero signal until an external probe on 2026-09-01.
confirmed.evidence: src/App.jsx:2,460 mounts `<Analytics />` but the Vercel API returns 404 'Web Analytics not found' (orchestrator fact — the project-level toggle was never enabled, so the component no-ops). api/_shared/log.js:25-27 — `log`, `log.warn`, `log.err` are bare console calls; `grep -n 'sentry|uptime|monitor|alert'` across src/main.jsx, src/App.jsx, package.json → nothing. Vercel Hobby runtime-log retention is on the order of hours (vercel.com/docs/limits), so the Sep-1 PrismaClientInitializationError would have aged out unseen. Supabase itself emails a pause warning ~1 week before and a confirmation after; those went to the org owner and were not acted on.
confirmed.impact: Availability incidents are invisible; revenue incidents (webhook 500s) are invisible; the Supabase restore-window clock runs silently. Any future paying customer's first contact will be a support email, not a dashboard.
confirmed.fix_hint: Minimum viable, all free: (1) Vercel dashboard → Analytics → Enable (the component is already mounted). (2) External uptime monitor (UptimeRobot/Better Stack free tier, 5-min interval) with three checks that would each have caught Sep-1: GET https://citation.today/api/auth/session must return HTTP 200 with JSON body `{}` or a user (a 500 = Prisma/auth down); GET /api/credits must return 401 (a 503/500 = DB down); GET /api/search/opencontext?q=test must return 200 with `results` — plus a keyword check that the body does NOT contain "error". (3) Route `log.err` through a webhook (Discord/Slack/email) or Vercel Log Drain (Pro) for any 5xx from /api/auth/handler and /api/stripe/webhook. (4) Forward Supabase org emails to a monitored inbox and add the daily DB keepalive from the P0 finding.

confirmed.evidence: pricing.js:73-75 packs $0.0010/$0.00083/$0.00067 per query. Comparators (2026): Tavily $8/1k PAYG, $5/1k Growth (https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-credits); Exa $7/1k (https://exa.ai/docs/reference/pricing); Brave $5/1k, free tier removed Feb 2026 (https://www.implicator.ai/brave-drops-free-search-api-tier-puts-all-developers-on-metered-billing/); Perplexity Sonar $5-14/1k + tokens (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing); SerpAPI $9-25/1k (https://apiserpent.com/blog/serpapi-pricing-explained); Consensus API $0.10/call by application (https://consensus.app/home/api/). Upstream: OpenAlex $1/1k search calls (live header X-RateLimit-Cost-USD: 0.001). Free substitutes: openags/paper-search-mcp MIT, 2,563 stars/255 forks (GitHub API 2026-08-17), 22 sources incl. OpenAlex, Crossref, DOAJ, BASE, Europe PMC, CORE, installable via PyPI/Smithery/npx (https://github.com/openags/paper-search-mcp); 8+ OpenAlex MCP servers (https://github.com/topics/openalex). OpenCite repo: 0 stars, 0 forks.
confirmed.impact: At list price, 1,000 pack buyers/month are needed to gross $10k, while each query loses money on OpenAlex alone; the free web app plus free MIT MCPs remove any reason for a scholarly-only developer to pay. Revenue potential of path (b) is near zero at this price.
confirmed.fix_hint: Reprice to cost-plus: e.g. $5/1k (still the cheapest metered search API by 30-70%), minimum pack $10 = 2k queries; charge 2 credits for heritage-tier fan-out. Sell what the free MCPs lack (heritage/Islamicate sources, citation formats, coverage-honest refunds, hosted/no-install) rather than competing on OpenAlex wrapper price.

OpenCITE does NOT currently pay OpenAlex anything: no OPENALEX key exists anywhere in api/ (serverKeys.js injects only Europeana/DPLA/Smithsonian; openalex.js:32 sends only &mailto), so the server rides the ANONYMOUS pool. Live OpenAlex headers today (X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000, Credits-Used: 10/search, Cost-USD: 0.001) + docs (help.openalex.org/access/pricing, /example-costs) mean: anonymous = $0.10/day = 100 search calls/day per IP; a free key = $1/day = 1,000 searches/day; beyond that $1/1k searches PAYG. So the margin is not negative today (usage is under the free allowance and zero traffic), but (a) prod as deployed can serve only ~50 all-tier API queries/day before OpenAlex 429s -> adapter throws -> coverage-prorated discount, i.e. a single 10k pack (~333 queries/day over a month) cannot be fulfilled at full coverage without at least a free OpenAlex key; (b) above ~500 all-tier queries/day the unit margin goes negative as the finding says, and worse than stated (2x). The docs/wiki/02-Adapters/capability-dossiers/openalex.md:198 figure of "10,000 requests/day anon" is stale by 10x for search calls.

Refutation attempt: the claim "each query loses money on OpenAlex alone" is FALSE as stated — grep of api/ finds no OPENALEX_API_KEY and openalex.js:31-32 only appends api_key from per-user settings (never set server-side), so OpenCITE pays $0 and is on the anonymous allowance; there is no cash loss today. But the corrected picture is worse in two ways: (1) all-tier queries make TWO OpenAlex search calls (OPENALEX + CURATED, curatedJournals.js:19 serverSafe:true; double-call deferred per sprint_log_v0_44 D-8), so marginal upstream at scale is $0.002/query vs ~$0.00094 net revenue; (2) the anonymous pool caps prod at ~100 OpenAlex searches/day (~50 all-tier API queries/day) before 429s degrade coverage, so even one 10k pack buyer cannot be served at full coverage as deployed. It is not moot; it is downstream of the P0s. Hence P2, not P1: a launch-decision plus an ops item (provision a free OpenAlex key at minimum), not a live defect. LENS 3 (novelty): Not in the working tree (no OpenAlex key, no repricing), not tracked in findings.json (no pricing/unit-economics entry; only F-315 PricingPanel currentPlan), not in sprint_log_v0_44 (D-8 defers the double-call without costing it) or v0_45 (only allowance-copy wording, pricing.js:81-82). confirmed.title: Zero discoverability: MCP is stdio-only and npm-private, OpenAPI/docs are not served, domain is unindexed
confirmed.claim: No channel through which an agent developer could find or install the OpenCITE API/MCP exists today; every 2026 directory requires either a public remote MCP endpoint (Claude/ChatGPT) or a published package (Smithery/npm), and the site itself has no API docs page.
confirmed.evidence: mcp/package.json:4 '"private": true' (npm refuses to publish); mcp/src/server.js:19,87-91 StdioServerTransport only, no Streamable HTTP; `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencite%2fmcp` -> {"error":"Not found"}; `curl https://citation.today/openapi.json` and `/docs` return the SPA index.html (vercel.json:13 catch-all rewrite) so the OpenAPI spec generated by `npm run print-schemas` (mcp/README.md:88-98) is never published; public/robots.txt welcomes GPTBot/ClaudeBot but WebSearch `site:citation.today` returns no indexed pages. Claude directory: remote HTTPS + streamable HTTP/SSE + OAuth 2.0 + Team/Enterprise org; local MCPB needs a privacy policy ('Missing or incomplete privacy policies result in immediate rejection') and docs/wiki/11-Legal/Legal-Overview.md:52 shows L2 Privacy Policy 'not started' (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/submission). ChatGPT: public production HTTPS MCP + verified identity (https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk/app-submission-guidelines). Smithery/Glama/PulseMCP accept claimed listings of published stdio packages or hosted HTTP endpoints (https://tallyfy.com/how-to-list-mcp-server-registry-smithery-glama-pulsemcp/).
confirmed.impact: Path (b) has a top-of-funnel of exactly zero: no developer can discover, install, or read the contract, independent of the key-mint UI gap. Prod logs confirm only orchestrator traffic.
confirmed.fix_hint: Cheapest order: (1) serve static /openapi.json and a /docs page (exclude from SPA rewrite); (2) set private:false, name it `opencite-mcp` (PyPI `opencite` is taken, R-NAME), npm publish, claim on Smithery/Glama/PulseMCP; (3) add a remote Streamable-HTTP MCP route (/api/mcp) with API-key auth for Cursor/Claude custom connectors (needs Vercel Pro or a function slot); (4) write the privacy policy, then apply to Claude directory via MCPB or remote.

votes.corrected_claim: No agent-developer discovery/install channel for the OpenCITE API/MCP exists: mcp/package.json:4 is "private": true (npm would refuse publish; neither @opencite/mcp nor opencite-mcp exists on the registry), mcp/src/server.js:19,87-95 wires only StdioServerTransport (no Streamable HTTP/SSE, so Claude/ChatGPT remote-connector directories are out of reach), the OpenAPI 3.1 spec produced by `npm run print-schemas` (mcp/README.md:88-98, apiContract.js WS4 gen) is never served — https://citation.today/openapi.json, /docs and /llms.txt all return the SPA index.html via the vercel.json:13 catch-all, and /api/openapi, /api/docs, /api/mcp are 404 — and the site has no API-docs page. Two corrections: (1) the domain is NOT wholly unindexed — a web search returns https://citation.today/ with its SEO title/description; only the SPA root is indexed and it says nothing about an API or MCP, so an agent developer searching for an MCP/scholarly grounding API still cannot find it; (2) a remote /api/mcp route does NOT need Vercel Pro — the tree has 8 Node functions (handler, checkout, citations, ids, search, search/[source], stripe/webhook, user/[resource]) + 4 Edge, so 4 Node slots remain under the 12-cap. Privacy-policy gate for Claude MCPB/directory listing is real: docs/wiki/11-Legal/Legal-Overview.md:52 L2 = not started.
votes.reasoning:
LENS 1 (factual): Verified every cited artifact read-only. mcp/package.json:4 `"private": true` (name @opencite/mcp, bin opencite-mcp). mcp/src/server.js imports only StdioServerTransport (line 19) and startStdioServer() (87-95) — no HTTP transport anywhere. `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencite%2fmcp` and `.../opencite-mcp` both → {"error":"Not found"}. `curl https://citation.today/openapi.json` → 200 text/html (SPA shell); /docs and /llms.txt likewise 200 text/html; /api/docs, /api/openapi, /api/mcp → 404. vercel.json:13 `/((?!api).*)` → index.html confirmed as the cause. mcp/README.md:88-98 documents print-schemas emitting openApi but nothing serves it; grep of src/ finds no docs/developer page (only the "For developers & AI agents" credit-pack card in Panels.jsx:265 and pricing comments). public/robots.txt welcomes GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot. Legal-Overview.md:52 L2 Privacy Policy = not started. Refutations found: (a) WebSearch for "OpenCITE citation.today" DOES return https://citation.today/ (title "OpenCITE — Free Open-Access Scholarly Search & Citation Tool") — the homepage is indexed; the `site:` query simply returned nothing useful. So "domain is unindexed" is overstated; corrected to "only the SPA root is indexed and carries no API/MCP content". (b) Fix hint (3) "needs Vercel Pro or a function slot" — `find api -name '*.js' -not -path '*/_shared/*'` shows 8 Node + 4 Edge files, so 4 Node slots are free on Hobby. Core claim stands with those corrections.

LENS 2 (impact): For MVP + first revenue in ~30 days this is real but sequenced behind harder blockers already established: Supabase paused (all auth/keys/checkout dead), no key-mint UI, plan=machine never assigned, Student unpurchasable. Publishing to npm/Smithery or serving openapi.json today would route developers into a dead end (401 with no way to get a key). First revenue in 30 days is far more plausible via the web Student/Pro subscription path, which needs none of this. Claude directory remote listing additionally requires a Team/Enterprise org and ChatGPT requires verified identity — multi-week approvals a solo founder cannot count on inside 30 days. However, path (b) (paid API/MCP, the product's stated monetization thesis and the entire premise of the v0.37 funnel plan) has literally zero top-of-funnel without this, and steps (1)-(2) of the fix (static openapi.json excluded from the rewrite, private:false + npm publish under opencite-mcp) are hours of work with no infra cost. Material, but P2 rather than P1 for the 30-day window: it cannot produce revenue until the key path and DB are restored, and the web path can produce first revenue without it.

LENS 3 (novelty): ESTABLISHED FACTS already state "@opencite/mcp is NOT on npm" and "no self-serve acquisition path", but this finding adds concrete depth not tracked anywhere: the `private:true` root cause, stdio-only transport as a structural exclusion from every remote-MCP directory, the generated-but-never-served OpenAPI spec (vercel.json catch-all swallowing /openapi.json,/docs,/llms.txt), the privacy-policy dependency for Claude directory submission (links to legal L2), and the indexing state. grep of docs/wiki/_machine/findings.json for npm publish/smithery/discover/openapi/private/streamable/directory finds no matching finding (only F-500 SDK pin and F-501 _text shape). sprint_log_v0_44.md and v0.45.md contain no mcp/npm/publish/openapi lines. The v0.37 plan (memory + wiki MCP-Server.md:103) assumes "ChatGPT's MCP hits /api/search" and that schema exports are "registration artifacts for ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini plugin listings" but includes no publish/listing/serve step — this finding exposes that unstated premise as a gap. Not fixed in the working tree (package.json/server.js/vercel.json unchanged per git diff --stat). adds_new = true.

Verdict: holds (fact true with two corrections, materially relevant, novel), severity lowered to P2.

confirmed.title: Non-refundable credits with no cancellation path; refunds and disputes never claw back credits
confirmed.claim: ToS §5 declares credits non-refundable and there is no user-facing cancel/portal, which conflicts with California ARL and EU Consumer Rights Directive obligations; and the webhook ignores charge.refunded / charge.dispute.* so a refunded or charged-back pack leaves the credits spendable.
confirmed.evidence: docs/wiki/11-Legal/Terms-of-Service.md:71 'Credits are non-refundable'. `grep -rn 'billingPortal|portal' api src` = no results; PricingPanel (src/components/Panels.jsx:183-290) has no cancel/manage button. api/stripe/webhook.js:124-198 handles only checkout.session.completed, RENEWAL_EVENTS, customer.subscription.updated/deleted, invoice.payment_failed — no charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, or credit reversal. Stripe checklist requires a cancellation policy for subscriptions; CA Bus. & Prof. Code 17602 requires online cancellation and affirmative consent to auto-renewal (non-compliant subscriptions are 'unconditional gifts'); EU CRD Art. 9/14 gives 14-day withdrawal on digital services with pro-rata refund.
confirmed.impact: Chargebacks reverse revenue while the customer keeps 10k-300k credits (double loss); statutory non-compliance in CA/EU can void subscription charges entirely; Stripe disputes without a posted policy are lost by default.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add a Stripe Customer Portal link (stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create) in the Plans panel; handle charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created in the webhook by decrementing the pack's credits (floor at 0) and flagging the account; rewrite ToS §5 to a lawful policy (14-day withdrawal for unused credits, pro-rata for subscriptions); add explicit auto-renewal consent text at checkout.

votes.corrected_claim: Two concrete gaps hold: (a) api/stripe/webhook.js:124-197 handles only checkout.session.completed, invoice.paid/payment_succeeded, customer.subscription.updated/deleted and invoice.payment_failed — there is no charge.refunded / charge.dispute.created branch and no clawback path anywhere (the only `decrement` in api/ is billing.js:32 per-search charge), so a refunded or charged-back pack (10k/60k/300k credits, plans.js:95-97) leaves the credits spendable; (b) there is no customer-facing cancel/manage path — `grep -rniE 'billingPortal|portal' api src` hits only unrelated strings (Azure Portal in .env.example, ENA Portal), api/checkout.js never creates a portal session, and PricingPanel (src/components/Panels.jsx:183-290) has only Subscribe/Buy CTAs. The ToS/consent parts are overstated: Terms-of-Service.md:71 actually reads 'non-refundable **except where required by law**' (a standard saving clause, not facially unlawful), the ToS is an unpublished DRAFT (no contract in force) and its refund stance is already tracked as Legal-Overview L5 ('confirm against Stripe + consumer law'); and Stripe-hosted Checkout in subscription mode displays the recurring-billing terms itself, though checkout.js sets no `consent_collection`/`custom_text` and there is no published ToS URL to consent to. Subscription cancellation initiated Stripe-side (dashboard/support) IS handled by the customer.subscription.deleted downgrade at webhook.js:186 — the gap is self-serve UI, not backend.
votes.reasoning: LENS 1 (factual): Read api/stripe/webhook.js in full — event branches at lines 124, 159, 173, 186, 193; no refund/dispute handling; `git diff --stat` on webhook.js/checkout.js is empty, so the deployed v0.44 tree equals committed code here (last touched a6d16b6 v0.39). Grep confirms no billingPortal/portal in api/ or src/ (only .env.example Azure Portal and ENA adapter text). PricingPanel lines 183-290 verified: subscribe/pack CTAs only, no cancel/manage. Terms-of-Service.md:71 verified but the finding drops the qualifier 'except where required by law', and the ToS is a draft (Legal-Overview.md:14 'DRAFT pending counsel review'), so the 'declares non-refundable in conflict with CA/EU law' framing is partly wrong — corrected above. Consent claim overstated because Stripe Checkout subscription mode shows renewal terms by default; no `consent_collection` in checkout.js though. Could not verify the 'Stripe checklist requires cancellation policy' assertion (needs Stripe dashboard); treated as plausible, not load-bearing. LENS 2 (impact): Today it is moot — Supabase is paused so the webhook itself throws PrismaClientInitializationError, zero traffic, no customers, no published ToS. But the stated goal is MVP + first revenue in ~30 days, which requires restoring the DB and selling packs/subscriptions; at that point (a) a refund/chargeback = double loss on up to 300k credits and (b) selling auto-renewing subscriptions to CA consumers without an online cancel path is a real 17602 exposure (albeit tiny in dollars at first revenue). Both fixes are cheap (a no-code Stripe portal link + ~30 lines in the webhook). Not P1: it is not a blocker to getting first revenue and the probability of a dispute in the first 30 days at ~zero traffic is low; it is a money-path integrity gap that belongs alongside v0.45. P2. LENS 3 (novelty): findings.json/_fragments contain no refund/dispute/portal finding; sprint_log_v0_45.md mentions the Stripe dispute window only for journal retention (D-2), not dispute handling or a portal; sprint_log_v0_44.md has nothing. The ToS §5 portion is already tracked (Legal-Overview L5) and overlaps the ESTABLISHED FACT 'ToS is DRAFT', but the webhook clawback gap and the missing self-serve cancel/portal path are new, concrete, code-level findings not previously ledgered. holds = true with severity lowered to P2 and the ToS/consent sub-claims corrected.

confirmed.title: Billable serverSafe set includes sources whose terms forbid commercial/origin-blind resale
confirmed.claim: 24 adapters are serverSafe (billable to paid/all-tier plans) but TOS-items.md reviewed only 5; at least Internet Archive, BASE, BnF, Thaqalayn, Open Library and relayed PubMed abstracts conflict with a paid, origin-blind API that strips attribution.
confirmed.evidence: `grep -l 'serverSafe: true' src/adapters/**/*.js | wc -l` = 24 vs the D-table in docs/wiki/99-Archive/TOS-items.md:79-85 covering only Smithsonian/DPLA/Europeana/CORE/NDLI; D5 (line 68) says no source ships into the billable set unreviewed. Internet Archive ToS (archive.org/about/terms.php, quoted in IA forum post 1101677): access to Collections 'granted for scholarship and research purposes only' — src/adapters/extensions/internetArchive.js:165 serverSafe:true, hits be-api.us.archive.org FTS (line 64). BASE: API is key/IP-gated and offered 'for non-commercial services' (api.base-search.net; searxng issue #5283) — src/adapters/extensions/base.js:32 serverSafe:true, line 44 calls the interface. BnF catalogue SRU metadata under Etalab Licence Ouverte requiring the source 'Bibliothèque nationale de France' be cited (api.bnf.fr CGU) — src/adapters/extensions/bnfApi.js:18,25; origin-blind contract (TOS-items B1/D6) forbids exactly that attribution. Thaqalayn: src/adapters/extensions/thaqalayn.js:22 calls www.thaqalayn-api.net, a third-party GPL-3.0 scraper (gh api repos/MohammedArab1/ThaqalaynAPI) of thaqalayn.net whose texts carry no reuse license ('educational and academic purposes only', thaqalayn.com/about). NCBI: adapter efetches abstracts (ncbi.js:62,80) and publicResult.js:43 relays `abstract` in the paid response; NLM policy: 'NLM does not claim the copyright on the abstracts in PubMed; however, journal publishers or authors may.' Open Library API: 'not intended to serve as ... high-traffic commercial infrastructure' (openlibrary.org/developers/api) — openLibrary.js:27 serverSafe:true.
confirmed.impact: Paid customers are sold content OpenCITE has no right to resell without attribution; an upstream block (IA/BASE/BnF revoking access to the shared prod egress) removes the source for every customer at once; publisher copyright claims on relayed abstracts create takedown/DMCA exposure with no designated agent.
confirmed.fix_hint: Apply the D6 filter to all 24 sources and record each in TOS-items.md; flip serverSafe to false for IA, BASE, BnF, Thaqalayn, Open Library (or obtain written licenses); drop `abstract` from the paid contract for NCBI-origin cards or truncate to snippet; keep those sources browser-only like CORE/NDLI.

confirmed.title: Personal data stored with no privacy policy, no deletion path, and analytics contradicting the 'No tracking' claim
confirmed.claim: OpenCITE stores Google OAuth refresh/access/id tokens, email, name, avatar, search history, library, Stripe customer ids and encrypted third-party API keys with no privacy notice, no account-deletion or export endpoint, while README claims 'No tracking' and the live bundle loads Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights.
confirmed.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:73-77 Account.refresh_token/access_token/id_token stored as plaintext @db.Text; :20-23 email/name/image; :109-119 search_history (query per user); :123-134 library_items; :26 stripe_customer_id; :45 settings encrypted blob (api/_shared/handlers/settings.js:5-7). api/user/[resource].js:20 HANDLERS = credits/history/keys/library/settings only — no delete-account or data export; history/library DELETE exist but the User/Account rows and Stripe link cannot be erased by the user. README.md:7 'No account required. No tracking.' vs src/App.jsx:2-3,460-461 mounting <Analytics/> and <SpeedInsights/>; live bundle contains '_vercel/insights', '_vercel/speed-insights', 'va.vercel-scripts'. Legal-Overview.md:52 L2 Privacy Policy 'not started'. Google OAuth production policy requires a homepage with linked privacy policy and ToS, and the same policy URL on the consent screen (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/policies).
confirmed.impact: GDPR Art. 13/17/20 and CCPA notice/deletion rights are unmet for EU/CA users the moment money changes hands (Stripe transactions expand the data set); Google can flag the OAuth app as unverified or suspend it, killing the only sign-in and therefore checkout; the false 'No tracking' statement is a deceptive-practice exposure.
confirmed.fix_hint: Publish a privacy policy naming Stripe, Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights, Supabase, Google OAuth and each upstream; add DELETE /api/user/account (cascade via Prisma onDelete, Stripe customer delete, subscription cancel) and a JSON export; either remove Analytics/SpeedInsights or correct README; set the privacy URL on the Google consent screen.

confirmed.title: Pre-commit hook blocks the v0.44 commit: machine-map --check fails with 32 problems (not 15)
confirmed.claim: The v0.44 working tree cannot be committed through the normal path: any commit that stages docs/wiki/ triggers `build-machine-map.mjs --check`, which currently exits 1 with 32 dangling-ref problems, so the sprint's acceptance criterion (sprint_log_v0_44.md:87) is unmet and the commit is blocked.
confirmed.evidence: `node scripts/wiki/build-machine-map.mjs --check` → "✗ 32 problem(s)" (run 2026-09-04 on working tree; orchestrator's ESTABLISHED FACTS said 15 — corrected). `.githooks/pre-commit:10-13` runs the non-check build then `--check` and exits 1 on failure when `git diff --cached` matches `^docs/wiki/`; `git config core.hooksPath` → `.githooks` (installed by package.json:12 `prepare`). scripts/wiki/build-machine-map.mjs:218 `process.exit(1)` only in --check mode; :228 the non-check run merely warns, so hook step 1 rewrites `_machine/*.json` (manifest.json `problems:0` → 32) and stages them before step 2 fails. Classification of the 32: 1 UNCURATED module (`src/adapters/_shared/contentMatch.js`, no fragment record); 14 curated module paths missing on disk (6 quarantined v0.44 adapters/routes bdh/britishLibrary/mexicana + api/search/{bl,bdh,mexicana}.js; ScoreExplainer.jsx; 7 engine modules scoring/rrf/semantic/synonyms/embed.worker/synonyms.worker/useSemanticRerank); 13 finding→unknown-module refs (F-106, F-200×2, F-201, F-202, F-204, F-205×2, F-207, F-209×2, F-408, F-409); 2 finding wiki-note-missing (F-205 → Semantic-Rerark.md, F-207 → Synonyms-Vocab.md); 2 module wiki-note-missing (constants.vocabulary → Synonyms-Vocab.md, lib.goldSetMetrics → Ranking-Scoring.md#gold-set-metrics). sprint_log_v0_44.md:3 Status EXECUTING, :90-92 Actuals empty, :67 T7 'Findings fragments: ranking findings → moot; F-405 → fixed; corpse adapters → quarantined. Rebuild machine map' — not done (see fragment statuses below).
confirmed.impact: Shahbaz cannot commit the tree that production is already running without bypassing the hook (`--no-verify`), which would commit a machine twin whose manifest lies (`problems:0`) — or the commit silently never happens and main stays at v0.43.1 while prod runs v0.44, keeping the Dependabot-merge regression trap armed.
confirmed.fix_hint: Edit the SSOT fragments, not generated JSON: (a) delete/`quarantined` the 14 module records in adapters/backend/frontend/pipeline.modules.json; (b) re-point F-106/F-408/F-409 to quarantine ids or drop `modules`; (c) restatus F-200/F-201/F-202/F-204/F-205/F-207/F-209 to `moot` with `wiki: 03-Search-Pipeline/Known-Defects.md`; (d) F-405 → fixed (api/_shared/handlers/settings.js:14,53 uses parseBody); (e) add a contentMatch record; (f) fix constants.vocabulary / lib.goldSetMetrics wiki refs (or delete goldSetMetrics if orphaned). Then `--check` passes and the hook regenerates twin + mirror automatically.

Two corrections: (a) the claim that step 1 "stages them before step 2 fails" is wrong — nothing is staged until :15, so the twin is rewritten in the working tree only; (b) "15" vs "32" is not a contradiction — 15 is precisely the finding-reference subset, 32 is the total. LENS 2 (impact): Not on the money path; DB paused; zero traffic; the hook itself documents a one-flag bypass (:7 `--no-verify`) and the fix is ~1 hour of fragment edits. But committing the v0.44 tree is a prerequisite to closing the main!=prod / Dependabot regression trap, which is on the 30-day path, and the hook turns an unmet acceptance line into a hard stop on the very first `git commit` — so it is material, but P2 not P1. LENS 3 (novelty): ESTABLISHED FACTS already record that --check fails (15 refs) and the fragment drift; sprint_log_v0_44 T7 + Acceptance already prescribe the same core fix (restatus ranking findings, F-405 fixed, quarantine corpse adapters, rebuild). New depth: (1) the pre-commit hook makes this a commit blocker that fires on the already-staged index, not just an unmet checklist item; (2) the full 32 count with classification, including two items T7 as written would NOT fix (uncurated contentMatch.js record; constants.vocabulary / lib.goldSetMetrics wiki refs to deleted pages) — so T7 alone leaves --check red; (3) the --no-verify hazard of committing a manifest that says problems:0. Verdict: holds, downgraded to P2.
