confirmed.title: Cache key omits `cite` formats: a cache hit is billed but ignores the caller's requested citation formats
confirmed.claim: cacheKey excludes `cite`, and the cached `results` were rendered with the ORIGINAL caller's citeFormats, so a later caller requesting cite=bibtex,ris pays the same charge and receives cards without those fields (or with someone else's).
confirmed.evidence: api/search.js:265-271 cacheKey({query,sources,limit,authors,format}) — no citeFormats; api/_shared/cache.js:28-35 confirms the key inputs; api/search.js:405 `renderCard(r, citeFormats)` runs only on the miss path; :412-423 caches the rendered `results`; :275-280 hit path returns `...cached` unchanged after charging via chargeForBand.
confirmed.impact: Paid response does not match the request contract; MCP/agent callers relying on bibtex/ris will see intermittent absence depending on who searched first within the 6h TTL.
confirmed.fix_hint: Either include `cite` in the cache key, or cache the pre-render `limited` records and render per request (preferred — one cache entry, correct output).

confirmed.title: No handling of refunds, disputes, or delayed-payment completion: credits are granted on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status
confirmed.claim: The webhook grants pack credits/plan on checkout.session.completed unconditionally and ignores charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/failed, so a refunded or disputed purchase keeps its credits and a delayed-notification payment is fulfilled before funds arrive.
confirmed.evidence: api/stripe/webhook.js:124-152 no `obj.payment_status` check; :34 RENEWAL_EVENTS and the type checks at :124,159,173,186,193 are the full handled set; Stripe fulfillment docs: 'Check the payment_status property to determine if it requires fulfillment' and delayed methods 'generate a checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded event when payment succeeds later'. Whether delayed methods are enabled on the account is unknown (inference on that half).
confirmed.impact: Operator issues a refund in the dashboard → customer keeps 10k–300k credits (double loss); a lost dispute likewise. Delayed-method buyer (if enabled) gets credits on 'unpaid'.
confirmed.fix_hint: Gate the pack grant on `payment_status === 'paid'`; handle async_payment_succeeded identically; on charge.refunded / dispute funds_withdrawn decrement credits (clamped at 0) and log; document a manual clawback procedure until then.

confirmed.title: Student plan is unpurchasable and the UI dead-ends: nothing ever sets is_student_verified
confirmed.claim: checkout returns 403 needs_student_verification for every user because no code path, admin tool, or provider writes is_student_verified; the PricingPanel shows the raw error with no verification route.
confirmed.evidence: grep is_student_verified|student_verified_at across api/ src/ scripts/ mcp/ → only the READ at api/checkout.js:59-60; prisma/schema.prisma:36-37 columns exist with @default(false); src/components/Panels.jsx:203 `setNotice(res?.error || …)` just displays 'Student verification required before subscribing'; pricing.js:49 CTA 'Verify & subscribe'.
confirmed.impact: A public plan that cannot be bought; users who try see an unactionable error. Also means the $5 rail has never been exercised end-to-end.
confirmed.fix_hint: Hide the Student card until a verification path exists (or add an admin toggle handler under api/user/[resource].js that sets is_student_verified for allowlisted admins).

confirmed.title: Keyed DPLA/Smithsonian shim routes accept a spoofed Sec-Fetch-Site header — project API quota burnable from curl
confirmed.claim: requireInternalOrigin trusts the literal value of `Sec-Fetch-Site` (only browsers refuse to let page JS set it; any non-browser client sets it freely), so a one-line curl obtains real keyed results from DPLA and Smithsonian on the project's keys with no auth, no rate limit and no metering.
confirmed.evidence: requireInternalOrigin.js:27-31 `const site = h["sec-fetch-site"]; if (site) ok = site === "same-origin" || site === "same-site"` — header value is not verifiable server-side. Live: `curl -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" "https://citation.today/api/search/dpla?q=abraham%20lincoln"` → 200 with real DPLA records (2147 bytes); `curl -H "Referer: https://citation.today/" ".../api/search/smithsonian?q=lincoln"` → 200 with real Smithsonian records; without headers → 403. api/search/[source].js:35-48 has no limiter. Smithsonian runs on api.data.gov (documented default 1,000 req/hour/key). Europeana returned `EUROPEANA_API_KEY not configured` (env unset — matches memory).
confirmed.impact: An attacker can exhaust the Smithsonian hourly quota in minutes, after which SMITHSONIAN throws inside the paid /api/search fan-out (search.js:323-327): every 'all'-tier customer loses that source, the coverage band drops to near-full (0.99×) until the per-instance breaker opens after 5 failures (adapterHealth.js:24), and repeated abuse risks api.data.gov revoking the key. DPLA has no published hard cap but the same relay applies.
confirmed.fix_hint: Treat the guard as what the code comment admits it is (soft) and add a real control: per-IP KV limiter on api/search/[source].js (reuse checkRateLimit with a small anonymous plan), plus a short-TTL server cache keyed on (source,q,offset) so repeats never reach upstream; optionally require the SPA to send a same-origin nonce minted by /api/auth/csrf.

confirmed.title: API-key auth performs DB reads and writes BEFORE rate limiting; invalid keys are never throttled
confirmed.claim: Every /api/search, /api/citations, /api/ids request with any x-api-key does a Prisma SELECT (and for valid keys a fire-and-forget UPDATE of last_used_at) before checkRateLimit runs; the 401 path for bad keys and the 400 paths for bad format/sources return before the limiter, so an attacker can drive unbounded Postgres traffic through the pgBouncer pool with no credential at all.
confirmed.evidence: search.js:167 `resolveApiKey(req)` (apiAuth.js:65-77: findUnique + `prisma.apiKey.update({last_used_at})`) → 401 at :169; format 400 at :197; sources 400 at :215; rate limit only at :255. Same ordering in meter.js:32-37 (authAndLimit: resolveApiKey then checkRateLimit). resolveSessionAdmin (apiAuth.js:96-102) adds a second SELECT on the sessions table for any request carrying a session cookie. Rate limiter itself is fail-open and KV-backed (ratelimit.js:45; kv.js:10-13) — if KV_REST_API_URL is unset in prod (unknown; .env.example:68 blank) the fallback is per-instance memory (ratelimit.js:20-28), multiplied by Vercel instance count.
confirmed.impact: Supabase free/pro pooler has a small connection budget; a cheap 401-spray exhausts it and cascades into sign-in, /api/credits, checkout and the paid search path (all share the same Prisma client) — a full-service DoS without an account. Valid free keys additionally generate one UPDATE per request regardless of the 30/min limit.
confirmed.fix_hint: Run a cheap per-IP KV limiter BEFORE any DB touch (apply to the 401 path); move the last_used_at stamp after checkRateLimit and debounce it (e.g. only if older than 60 s); reject malformed keys (not matching /^oc_live_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$/) before hashing/lookup; confirm KV is provisioned in prod so the shared limiter is actually active.

confirmed.title: `?key=` query-string API keys leak bearer credentials into Vercel request logs, proxies and browser history
confirmed.claim: presentedKey() accepts the customer API key as a URL query parameter; URLs (including query strings) are recorded in Vercel runtime/request logs, Web Analytics, corporate proxies and browser history, and can be sent as Referer from a browser client — none of which happens with the header form the MCP client uses.
confirmed.evidence: apiAuth.js:43-45 `req.headers?.["x-api-key"] || firstParam(req.query?.key)`; documented at search.js:32. Live: `curl "https://citation.today/api/search?q=test&key=oc_live_bogus"` → 401 (parameter is parsed). mcp/src/client.js:42 only ever uses the header. Inference (0.7): Vercel runtime logs display the full request path including the query string, so a key used this way is retained in the log store for the retention window.
confirmed.impact: A leaked key is a bearer credential to the customer's prepaid credits (no origin/IP binding — /api/search sends ACAO:* with x-api-key allowed, search.js:150-152); support staff or anyone with Vercel log access would see customer keys in the clear.
confirmed.fix_hint: Drop `?key=` support (header-only) before onboarding paying customers; if a query form must exist, redact `key` from logging and document it as discouraged; consider key restrictions (allowed IPs/origins) as a later feature.

confirmed.title: Unbounded `;` multi-term fan-out: one credit can trigger thousands of upstream requests
confirmed.claim: q is split on ';' with no cap on the number of terms, and each eligible adapter runs one upstream request per term inside Promise.all, so a single 1-credit request with N terms costs N×(adapters) upstream calls — the amplifier is bounded only by URL length.
confirmed.evidence: search.js:250 `const terms = q.split(";")...` (no length check); :306-312 `Promise.all(terms.map((t) => runSearch(adapter, t, settings, ...)))` per adapter; 'all' tier has 24 serverSafe adapters (grep serverSafe: true → 24 files). Live: a 1,500-term q (≈3 KB URL) is accepted by the platform (returns 401 for lack of key, not 414). Same split in src/hooks/useSearch.js:43 for the browser path. Per-adapter 12 s timeout (search.js:66) does not limit request count, only latency.
confirmed.impact: A free-tier key (30 req/min) can generate ~30×1500×4 = 180k upstream calls/min against OpenAlex/Crossref/DOAJ under the project's OPENCITE_MAILTO polite-pool identity, getting the project throttled or blocked and degrading coverage (and thus revenue via freeBelowBand refunds) for all paying customers; also inflates function duration toward the Hobby limit.
confirmed.fix_hint: Cap terms (e.g. max 5) and total q length (e.g. 512 chars) in apiContract.js and enforce in search.js before auth-independent work; charge per term or reject over-cap with 400; mirror in useSearch.

confirmed.title: AbortSignal.timeout hard dependency breaks every adapter on Safari/iOS < 16 (no polyfill, no browserslist)
confirmed.claim: fetchWithTimeout calls AbortSignal.timeout() unconditionally; on Safari 15.x / iOS 15 it is undefined, so the call throws TypeError synchronously before fetch is issued. Every adapter (direct fetches and both proxiedFetch branches) now routes through it, so those users get an error in every section and zero results.
confirmed.evidence: src/adapters/_shared/proxy.js:19 `return fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS), ...options });`; proxy.js:50 and :73 wrap both proxiedFetch branches; `grep -rn "[^a-zA-Z_.]fetch(" src/adapters | grep -v fetchWithTimeout\|proxiedFetch` → no remaining bare fetch (every adapter is affected). `grep -n browserslist\|target\|engines package.json vite.config.js` → nothing (Vite default target = es2020/safari14). Live bundle contains `AbortSignal.timeout` ×1 (shipped). AbortSignal.timeout shipped in Safari 16.0 (Sept 2022), Chrome 103, Firefox 100; Node ≥17.3 so the Vercel Node 24 fan-out is fine.
confirmed.impact: Users on iOS 15 / macOS Safari 15 (a small but non-zero share, roughly low single-digit percent of Safari traffic) see 'AbortSignal.timeout is not a function' style errors in every source and an empty results page — a total product failure for that segment with no fallback.
confirmed.fix_hint: Guard once: `const timeoutSignal = ms => typeof AbortSignal.timeout === 'function' ? AbortSignal.timeout(ms) : (() => { const c = new AbortController(); setTimeout(() => c.abort(), ms); return c.signal; })();` in proxy.js, or add a browserslist/`build.target` that documents the floor.

confirmed.title: Public API contract broken (score/lowConfidence removed) with no version field, header, or deprecation path
confirmed.claim: D-7 removed two documented result fields and one envelope field from /api/search in place; the contract has no version identifier anywhere, no deprecation window, and the MCP package docs/description still advertise the old shape.
confirmed.evidence: apiContract.js RESULT_FIELDS (lines ~92-96) and RESPONSE_SHAPE (~101-107) no longer list score/lowConfidence; `grep -n version\|deprecat api/_shared/apiContract.js api/search.js` → no matches (no versioning exists). publicResult.js:50-51 emits citedBy then citations (no score). Consumers: mcp/README.md:22 still says the envelope returns `lowConfidence`; mcp/package.json:6 description still says 'deduped, ranked'; mcp/src/schema.js:90-91 and :117-118 keep dead `lowConfidence`/`score` branches (harmless — schema is derived from RESULT_FIELDS/RESPONSE_SHAPE, so the generated tool schema no longer advertises them). docs/wiki/04-Backend-API/Search-Endpoint.md:34 documents the removal. api/_shared/cache.js: cacheKey() has no version component and DEFAULT_TTL 6h, so for 6h after the deploy cached bodies with score/lowConfidence and BM25F order were still served (expired now).
confirmed.impact: Today the blast radius is ~zero (established: no self-serve key path, no external consumers), but the API is the paid product and it has no mechanism to evolve without silently breaking clients; the first paying integrator would be broken by the next contract change and the MCP package would misdescribe its own output.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add `version: "2"` (or a date) to API_CONTRACT and echo it as `X-OpenCITE-API-Version`; include the version in cacheKey(); fix mcp/README.md:22 and mcp/package.json:6; delete the dead branches in mcp/src/schema.js:90-91,117-118.

confirmed.title: Silent-swallow: shim-route adapters ignore the route's `error` field, so the broken Gallica edge route renders as 'no results'
confirmed.claim: The Gallica adapter (and the OpenContext/OpenEdition/DPLA/Smithsonian shim adapters) only checks r.ok; the edge routes fail-soft with HTTP 200 + `error`, so a permanently broken upstream/route is displayed as an empty section and counts as full coverage rather than a failure.

confirmed.impact: Gallica has been dead-on-arrival since the edge route shipped, yet every user who enables it sees 'no matches' instead of an error, and neither the client circuit-breaker signal nor coverage/billing (server fan-out excludes it, so no billing effect) reflects the failure; the same pattern will hide the next broken shim.
confirmed.fix_hint: In each shim adapter: `if (data.error) throw new Error(data.error)` (mirror europeana.js:49). For Gallica itself, replace DOMParser in api/search/gallica.js with the regex/xmlUtils approach the other edge routes use, or move it to the Node [source].js shim.

confirmed.title: Auth nag UX: modal and tooltip stack on first visit, the 'after 3 searches' nag is unreachable dead code, and neither mentions Plans/API

Copy: Layout.jsx:86 "Sign in to sync your favourites and search history", :343 "Sign in to sync your saved library and search history".

confirmed.claim: On 2026-09-04 loc.gov search returned 503 after ~45s from the probe IP and the prod edge proxy hit Vercel's 25s kill (504) for the Chronicling America URL; LC_DATASETS (direct fetch, serverSafe) and CHRONICLING_AMERICA both count as failed adapters on the API, moving the all-tier band to 'high' (0.95x), and the proxy itself has no AbortSignal so a hung upstream consumes the full edge function budget.

confirmed.claim: The Gallica edge route parses SRU XML with DOMParser, which does not exist in Vercel Edge, so every Gallica browser search returns the error envelope; the upstream itself works (644 hits live) and src/adapters/_shared/xmlUtils.js already provides sruTotal/sruRecords/dcOne/dcAll used by ONB/BnF.
confirmed.evidence: Prod: `GET https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` -> 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"}`; direct SRU `gallica all "ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> numberOfRecords 644. Code: api/search/gallica.js:48 `new DOMParser()`, :45 comment admits it; xmlUtils.js:1-16 header says the helpers exist precisely because 'DOMParser is not reliably available in all Edge runtime contexts'. Adapter src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:29 ignores `data.error`.
confirmed.impact: BnF Gallica (15M items, one of the few full-text heritage sources) is dead in the only runtime it is wired to; user sees an empty section with no error.
confirmed.fix_hint: Replace DOMParser in api/search/gallica.js with the xmlUtils DC helpers (the Edge route cannot import src/, so inline or move xmlUtils under api/_shared); surface `data.error` in the shim adapter.

confirmed.title: Coverage billing is asymmetric and now overstated: one OpenAlex timeout = free query, while dead-but-200 sources are counted as covered
confirmed.claim: Corpus-weighted coverage makes the free tier a coin-flip on OpenAlex (25% of all-tier, 60% of free-tier weight): its single timeout yields band 'limited' (0 credits), Crossref's yields 'partial' (0.5x), whereas five heritage sources failing together move the band by 1%; and because failure is defined as 'threw', the five adapters that return 200-with-nothing (BASE 30.16%, MET, PANGAEA, THAQALAYN, OPENCONTEXT-n/a) are counted as covered, so 'full' is reported and charged for a library where >30% of the declared weight is unreachable.
confirmed.evidence: cov.mjs against the live registry (coverage.js computeCoverage/bandFor): FREE OpenAlex fails -> cov 0.3976 'limited' x0; FREE Crossref fails -> 0.6265 'partial' x0.5; FREE DOAJ fails -> 0.9759 'high'; ALL OpenAlex fails -> 0.7487 'partial'; ALL MET+THAQ+NU+DPUL+PANGAEA fail -> 0.9989 'near-full' x0.99; ALL every non-core fails -> 'limited' x0. coverage.js:47-48 'empty results is NOT a failure'; :18 FALLBACK_CORPUS=1 applies only to CORE/NDLI (not serverSafe, so irrelevant to the denominator). Live OpenAlex latency in probe: 4455ms vs ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_MS 12000 (api/search.js:66).
confirmed.impact: Revenue leaks whenever OpenAlex is slow (queries become free) yet customers are overcharged structurally because the denominator includes sources that can never answer; the band no longer measures what it claims.
confirmed.fix_hint: Treat 'zero results from a source whose upstream returned an error body' as failure (adapters throw on `error` keys); remove unreachable sources from serverSafe; consider capping any single source's weight (e.g. 40%) or using a query-hit-based signal instead of static corpusSize.

confirmed.title: NCBI E-utilities called without tool/email/api_key, 3 sequential-parallel calls per search against a shared 3 req/s per-IP budget
confirmed.claim: The NCBI adapter sends esearch + esummary + efetch (3 requests) per search with no `tool`, `email` or `api_key` parameters, so every server-side search consumes the entire 3 req/s anonymous per-IP allowance; on Vercel's shared egress IPs and at the machine plan's 300 req/min this guarantees 429s, and it violates NCBI's usage policy which asks for tool+email (idResolve.js does it correctly).
confirmed.evidence: ncbi.js:53 esearch URL, :61 esummary, :62 efetch -- none carry tool/email/api_key; grep shows NCBI_API_KEY is read only in api/ids.js:41 and api/search.js:341 (the default-off canonicalizer); src/lib/idResolve.js:29 DEFAULT_EMAIL='ops@citation.today' and :111 `email:` param -- the search adapter never received the same treatment. api/_shared/plans.js:68 machine rateLimit max 300/min.
confirmed.impact: NCBI throttling turns into 'failed adapter' events (3.72% weight) and, worse, IP-level blocks that also hit /api/ids; policy non-compliance risk for a commercial API.
confirmed.fix_hint: Append `&tool=opencite&email=<OPENCITE_MAILTO>` and `&api_key=${NCBI_API_KEY}` (10 req/s) in ncbi.js; add a tiny per-instance token bucket for eutils; consider Europe PMC (dossier Tier A) as the server-side biomedical source.

confirmed.title: Crossref/OpenAlex polite pool depends on OPENCITE_MAILTO being set; without it the server shares a 1 req/s Crossref pool (live-verified) and sends UA 'node'
confirmed.claim: Crossref and OpenAlex only get the polite pool when settings.crossrefEmail is non-empty, which on the API comes from ?mailto or process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO (unverified in Vercel) and in the browser defaults to ''; no User-Agent is set anywhere on the direct-fetch adapters, so server requests identify as Node's default UA.
confirmed.evidence: Live 2026-09-04: api.crossref.org without mailto -> `x-rate-limit-limit: 1, x-rate-limit-interval: 1s`; with `&mailto=ops@citation.today` -> `x-rate-limit-limit: 3`. Code: crossref.js:28 mailto conditional; openalex.js:30-31; curatedJournals.js:33-35; api/search.js:246 `process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO || DEFAULT_SETTINGS.crossrefEmail`; defaults.js:25 `crossrefEmail: ""`; fetchWithTimeout (proxy.js:18-20) adds no UA. Whether OPENCITE_MAILTO is set in prod could not be read (Vercel get_project does not expose env) -- inference 0.6 that it is unset given no runtime evidence.
confirmed.impact: If unset, all API customers share 1 req/s to Crossref (and OpenAlex's anonymous pool) per egress IP: the machine plan's 5 req/s cap alone would exceed it; every extra search also doubles OpenAlex load because CURATED is a second OpenAlex call.
confirmed.fix_hint: Set OPENCITE_MAILTO in Vercel prod; hard-code a fallback mailto + `User-Agent: OpenCITE/<ver> (https://citation.today; mailto:...)` in fetchWithTimeout for the server branch; verify with the x-rate-limit headers.

confirmed.title: titleFingerprint collapses every title-less record (sanitized to 'Untitled') into one, and merges same-title works with empty author/year
confirmed.claim: The fingerprint is `${normalizedTitle}|${year}|${firstAuthorSurname}`; sanitize() rewrites empty titles to 'Untitled' and heritage adapters frequently emit authors [] and year '', so all such records share the key 'untitled||' and the pooled dedup (dedupHighestScore) field-merges them into the first one (server) or drops them (browser); generic titles ('Introduction', 'Editorial', newspaper mastheads) from sources that emit no authors collide the same way. DOI normalization itself is correct.
confirmed.evidence: dedup.js:25-30 titleFingerprint; :136-140 merge into first keeper; src/adapters/_shared/base.js:28 `title: str(result.title) || "Untitled"`; adapters emitting authors: [] -- chroniclingAmerica.js:44, thaqalayn.js:35, api/search/opencontext.js:82, wikidata fallback; IA FTS mapFtsHit title fallback internetArchive.js:124 ('f_2171000'-style junk titles observed live); doiKey dedup.js:15-21 verified (lowercase, trims, strips doi.org prefix; note it does not strip a 'doi:' prefix or trailing punctuation). Logic-verified, not live-observed (no API key).
confirmed.impact: Legitimate distinct records vanish or are merged into a chimera (abstract/authors/subjects unioned from unrelated works) exactly for the metadata-poor heritage sources the all tier sells.
confirmed.fix_hint: Return null from titleFingerprint when the title is the 'Untitled' sentinel or shorter than ~3 tokens with no author/year; include source-agnostic secondary keys (url) before falling back to title.

confirmed.title: Gallica edge route is permanently dead: DOMParser does not exist in Vercel Edge runtime
confirmed.claim: api/search/gallica.js declares `runtime: 'edge'` and constructs `new DOMParser()` which is not available in the Edge V8 runtime, so every request returns the fail-soft error envelope and Gallica contributes zero results to every search.
confirmed.evidence: api/search/gallica.js:3 `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }`; :45-52 try `new DOMParser()` catch → `{ results: [], total: 0, error: 'DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime' }`. Live: `curl https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` → http=200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"}`. The other two edge shims are healthy: /api/search/opencontext?q=test → 200 `{"results":[],"total":0,"hasMore":false}`; /api/search/openedition?q=test → 200 with results. The code comment at :45 shows the author anticipated this and shipped anyway.
confirmed.impact: A listed source silently never returns results, and because the shim answers 200 the coverage/credit math and the UI treat it as a healthy-but-empty adapter — users and API customers pay for a source that cannot work.
confirmed.fix_hint: Either parse the SRU XML with a regex/lightweight tokenizer (the existing src/adapters/_shared/xmlUtils.js pattern) or move Gallica into the Node `api/search/[source].js` dispatcher (8 Node files today, 12 cap → slots available). Add a live smoke assertion so a shim that returns `error` on a fixed query fails the post-deploy check.

confirmed.title: Preview deployments have no database env at all — Dependabot 'green' builds prove nothing about runtime, and migrate.mjs burns three failing Prisma runs per preview
confirmed.claim: POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING (and by inference POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL) is scoped to Production only, so every preview build fails schema validation, runs the fallback anyway, and ships a bundle whose auth/credits/checkout/webhook code cannot execute; a READY preview therefore says nothing about whether @auth/core 0.41.3 or prisma-adapter 2.11.3 actually work.
confirmed.evidence: Build logs of dpl_DE31RrgR8RNxBm4GvYMTJ5hwHMEE and dpl_94wrsdgkHC956DPsfG9wkH4st6R9: `Error code: P1012 … Environment variable not found: POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING. --> prisma/schema.prisma:13` for `migrate deploy` AND again for the `db execute` fallback, then `[migrate] SQL apply failed — NOT baselining`, then the build completes and the deployment is READY. scripts/migrate.mjs:47-63 has no `VERCEL_ENV` guard. package.json:9 runs migrate.mjs unconditionally in `build`.

Preview URLs shared for review also mislead reviewers (auth UI is dead there for an unrelated reason).

confirmed.title: Digital sales with no tax collection or customer location capture
confirmed.claim: Checkout sessions are created with no automatic_tax, billing_address_collection or tax_id_collection, so VAT/GST/sales tax on cross-border digital services is neither charged nor tracked.

Stripe guidance: EU VAT applies to B2C digital services based on customer location from the first sale for non-EU sellers (stripe.com/guides/introduction-to-eu-vat-and-european-vat-oss); several US states tax SaaS.

confirmed.title: Upstream identification policies violated by spoofed or absent User-Agent and missing NCBI tool/email
confirmed.claim: Server-side requests either spoof a Chrome desktop User-Agent or send none, and NCBI E-utilities calls omit the required tool/email parameters, breaching NCBI, Open Library and Wikimedia access policies for automated clients.

Chrome/122' as User-Agent. src/adapters/extensions/ncbi.js:53,61,62 call esearch/esummary/efetch with no `tool=`/`email=`/`api_key=` (search.js:341 passes NCBI_API_KEY only to the env-gated canonicalizer, not the adapter). Only wikidata.js:7 sets a proper Api-User-Agent. OPENCITE_MAILTO is commented out in .env.example:77 so Crossref polite pool depends on an unverified prod env var.
confirmed.impact: A single IP block of Vercel's shared egress silently removes NCBI/Open Library/IA for every paying customer (TOS-items D2), while coverage-prorated billing still charges; UA spoofing weakens any good-faith defence in an upstream dispute.

confirmed.title: Gallica Edge route has returned a hard-coded 'DOMParser unavailable' error since 2026-05-21 and no finding tracks it
confirmed.claim: The Gallica per-source route runs on the Edge runtime and calls `new DOMParser()`, which the code itself predicts is unavailable; every request returns 200 with zero results, so Gallica has never worked in prod and the browser adapter that depends on it always shows nothing.
confirmed.evidence: api/search/gallica.js:3 `runtime: 'edge'`, :45 comment 'DOMParser may not exist in Vercel Edge V8', :48 `new DOMParser()`, :52 returns `{results: [], error: 'DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime'}` with status 200. `git log -- api/search/gallica.js` → 0c9b480 (05-29), 1918934 (05-26), 0d2751e (05-21). Live: `curl -s https://citation.today/api/search/gallica?q=test` → `{"results":[],"total":0,"error":"DOMParser unavailable in Edge runtime"} [200]` (opencontext/openedition edge routes return data). src/adapters/extensions/gallica.js:26 fetches this relative URL. `grep -niE 'gallica|DOMParser' docs/wiki/_machine/findings.json` → only F-112 (transport audit, v0.38 T8) and F-410; no finding for the breakage — v0.38 T8 audited this file's transport (findings.json:177) without noticing it never returns results.
confirmed.impact: Users see a dead source in every browser search (silent 0 results); the coverage/adapter-health story in the wiki counts Gallica as live; the v0.38 circuit-breaker cannot catch it because the route returns 200 not an error.
confirmed.fix_hint: Parse the SRU XML without DOMParser (regex or a tiny XML tokenizer already used in xmlUtils) or move the route into the Node `api/search/[source].js` dispatcher (does not add a function — the 12-function cap is already hit). Mint a finding id and add it to the ledger.

votes.reasoning: Lens 1 (refutation): every line cite checks out verbatim, but the central technical claim — that generated schemas "still emit lowConfidence and score" — is FALSE. Ran the generator functions directly (node --input-type=module, pure import chain, no build): 0 lowConfidence, 0 "score"; card/envelope property lists match the v0.44 contract; the tool description already carries the v0.44 "native relevance order, fairly interleaved" text. The stale parts are prose/strings only (README:85/:105/:22, server.js:13, openApiSpec :240/:243/:247, package.json:6, MCP-Server.md:17/:30/:99). Lens 2 (impact): @opencite/mcp is unpublished, no self-serve key path exists, and the DB is paused, so there are zero developer readers and nobody can be charged; the "trust-destroying while credits are charged" scenario cannot occur today. It is a ~20-minute prose fix that must precede any developer-facing publish of the paid API/MCP — on the revenue path but not blocking; P1 is inflated, P3 is honest. Lens 3 (novelty): ESTABLISHED FACTS already list schema.js/README lowConfidence and package.json "ranked"; sprint_log_v0_44.md T7 enumerates wiki pages to correct and MCP-Server.md is absent; sprint_log_v0_45.md has nothing on mcp/; findings.json only has F-500/F-501 for mcp/. The stale auth/billing prose, the OpenAPI anonymous security alternative and hard-coded strings, server.js:13, and the three MCP-Server.md contradictions are untracked — modest but real added depth. holds = true only under the corrected claim and at P3.

confirmed.title: Rate limit is per API key: a user with 10 active keys gets 10x their plan's burst cap
confirmed.claim: checkRateLimit is keyed on identity.keyId, and each user may hold 10 active keys, so the per-plan max is effectively multiplied by 10.
confirmed.evidence: api/search.js:255 and api/_shared/meter.js:37 `checkRateLimit(identity.keyId ?? clientIp(req), identity.plan)`; api/_shared/handlers/keys.js:53-55 cap is 10 active keys per user; ratelimit.js:41 key = `oc:rl:${identity}:${epoch}`.
confirmed.impact: Free plan 30/min becomes 300/min against upstream polite pools; 'Priority rate limits' (pricing.js:63) is not a real differentiator.
confirmed.fix_hint: Key the limiter on userId (fall back to keyId only for the master key).

confirmed.title: ApiUsage table is never written; there is no per-key usage record for support or disputes
confirmed.claim: The api_usage rollup declared as the analytics record has no writer anywhere, so the only trace of a spend is the mutated balance.
confirmed.evidence: grep apiUsage|api_usage across api/ src/ scripts/ → no matches outside prisma/ (schema.prisma:160-170, migration 20260530120000_billing:36-45); keys.js:24-27 lists only last_used_at (apiAuth.js:75-77).
confirmed.impact: Support cannot answer 'how many calls did my key make'; compounds the missing journal that sprint T1 addresses.
confirmed.fix_hint: Either write an upsert per successful charge (fits inside T1's journal transaction) or drop the model to stop advertising a record that does not exist.

confirmed.title: Post-checkout return is unhandled: balance/tier stay stale until a full reload
confirmed.claim: The success_url `/?checkout=success` (checkout.js:110) is not read anywhere in the client, and BillingContext only refetches on auth status/user id change.
confirmed.evidence: grep 'checkout=success|checkout' in src/App.jsx, src/components/*.jsx, src/hooks/*.js → no handler; BillingContext.jsx:31-56 effect deps `[status, user?.id]` only.
confirmed.impact: Buyer returns to an unchanged UI with old credit count — the first impression after paying is 'nothing happened', which drives refund requests.
confirmed.fix_hint: On mount, if `checkout=success` is present, poll /api/credits a few times over ~10 s and show a confirmation toast; strip the param.

confirmed.title: Concurrent first checkouts create duplicate Stripe customers; renewals under the orphaned customer never map to the user
confirmed.claim: Two parallel POST /api/checkout calls from a user with no stripe_customer_id both create a Customer; the last write wins, and any subscription created on the other customer resolves to no user on invoice events.
confirmed.evidence: api/checkout.js:86-98 read-then-create-then-update without a guard; api/stripe/webhook.js:63-73 resolveUserId falls back to `stripe_customer_id` lookup for invoice/subscription events (no client_reference_id there); F-416 path at webhook.js:109-115 only logs.
confirmed.impact: Rare (double-click), but the outcome is a paying subscriber who never receives monthly grants and whose cancellation never downgrades.
confirmed.fix_hint: Use `stripe.customers.create` with an idempotency key of the userId, or search existing customers by metadata.userId before creating; also make webhook.js:126 conditional on the column being null.

confirmed.title: Admin allowlist emails are shipped in the public JS bundle and tracked in the repo
confirmed.claim: VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS is inlined into the client bundle by design, and the real values are also committed in .env.local.example, so the exact Google accounts that unlock the unmetered admin plan, origin-revealing ?debug=1 and the admin console are public — the entire admin boundary is 'control of one of two named Gmail accounts'.
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/admin.js:3 `import.meta.env.VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS` (build-time inline). Live: `curl https://citation.today/assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js | grep -oE "[a-z0-9._-]+@gmail\.com"` → shahbaz.citationtoday@gmail.com, zabhahs11@gmail.com. Tracked: .env.local.example:6 same two addresses; docs/wiki-gh/99-Archive/architecture_report_v0_19.md:153. Server gate apiAuth.js:39-40 reads the same var at Node runtime (Vercel exposes all project env vars to functions, so it does work — established memory confirms admin path functions) and grants plan=admin on any DB session whose email matches (apiAuth.js:100-101).
confirmed.impact: Targeted phishing / OAuth-consent attacks against two known Google accounts; compromise of either yields unmetered all-tier search, origin-revealing debug output (breaks the product's origin-blind promise) and admin console access. Low likelihood today (zero traffic) but permanent once indexed.
confirmed.fix_hint: Move the allowlist server-side only (ADMIN_EMAILS, non-VITE) and have the client learn `isAdmin` from /api/credits (`tier: "admin"`) instead of a baked list; replace real addresses in .env.local.example with placeholders; enforce 2-step verification on the admin Google accounts.

confirmed.title: @auth/core 0.37.4 carries three July-2026 advisories (one Critical) — the Dependabot bump is security-motivated but non-exploitable in this config; do not take it via PR merge
confirmed.claim: @auth/core <0.41.3 is affected by CVE-2026-73420 (Critical 9.1, magic-link homoglyph account takeover), CVE-2026-73418 (High 7.5, getToken() DoS) and GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279 (Moderate, OAuth check cookies not provider-bound); OpenCITE uses none of the vulnerable paths, so the bump is hygiene — but merging the Dependabot PR would deploy GitHub main and regress prod to pre-v0.44.
confirmed.evidence: package.json:15 pins 0.37.4; package-lock resolves @auth/core 0.37.4 at root AND a nested 0.41.2 under @auth/prisma-adapter (two copies). Advisories: https://better-auth.com/blog/security-update-july-2026 , https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh (Email provider + default normalizeIdentifier required), https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj (requires direct getToken() call), https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279 (requires ≥2 OAuth providers). Non-exploitability: `grep -rn "getToken\|Email(\|providers/email" api src` → no matches; api/auth/handler.js:35-59 configures a single Google OIDC provider. No 2025-26 advisories found for @prisma/client 6.19.3 (lockfile) or stripe 17.7.0 (WebSearch, no hits). Established fact: pushing to main triggers a GitHub production deploy of the pre-v0.44 tree.
confirmed.impact: No current exploit path; residual risk only if an Email provider or a second OAuth provider (Apple/Microsoft are stubbed in handler.js:44-54) is enabled without upgrading. The operational risk is larger: a reflexive 'merge Dependabot' click regresses production.
confirmed.fix_hint: Bump @auth/core to 0.41.3 (and @auth/prisma-adapter 2.11.3, mcp sdk 1.30.0) in the working tree, deploy via CLI as usual, then close the Dependabot PRs; add a repo note/branch-protection that main is not the deploy source until the v0.44 tree is committed.

confirmed.title: OWN_VERCEL_HOST_RE trusts any `opencite*.vercel.app` — a namespace anyone can claim
confirmed.claim: isTrustedOrigin() accepts every host matching /^opencite[a-z0-9-]*\.vercel\.app$/; Vercel project subdomains are globally allocated, so a third party can deploy `opencite-evil.vercel.app` and be treated as a first-party origin for credentialed CORS, checkout success/cancel URLs and the shim-route Origin/Referer fallback.
confirmed.evidence: auth.js:22 regex; used by setCorsHeaders (auth.js:37-42, reflects origin + Allow-Credentials:true), checkout.js:31 (baseUrl → success_url/cancel_url), requireInternalOrigin.js:33-35. Live: `curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} https://opencite-evil.vercel.app/` → 404 (unclaimed, claimable). Mitigations that currently blunt it: session cookie is SameSite=lax (node_modules/@auth/core/lib/utils/cookie.js:52) so a cross-site fetch from the squatted origin carries no cookie; modern browsers send Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site which requireInternalOrigin checks first.
confirmed.impact: Today: low — needs a squatted project AND a browser that omits Sec-Fetch-Site or a future SameSite=None change; then it becomes credentialed CSRF against /api/keys (mint), /api/settings (read decrypted user keys) and a checkout redirect to an attacker page.
confirmed.fix_hint: Replace the regex with an exact list: `opencite.vercel.app` plus previews derived from process.env.VERCEL_URL / VERCEL_BRANCH_URL at runtime, or drop preview trust entirely in production.

confirmed.title: `sources=` validation is an unbilled, unthrottled catalog-enumeration oracle
confirmed.claim: A free-tier key can enumerate the server-side adapter catalog and tier membership for free: an unknown or out-of-tier ID yields 400 before rate-limiting or pre-authorization, while a valid ID yields 200 — contradicting the 'we never echo the internal source catalog' comment.
confirmed.evidence: search.js:205-218 (tier intersection → 400 'No valid sources selected') executes before checkRateLimit (:255) and preAuthorize (:286), so probing is unmetered and unlimited; api/search/[source].js:40 additionally echoes `Unknown source "<input>"`. Catalog IDs are guessable from the public SPA (adapter names are shown to browser users), so the oracle mostly reveals per-plan tier membership.
confirmed.impact: Minor information leak (which sources a plan tier includes) and another pre-limiter request path that reaches the DB via resolveApiKey first (see pre-auth finding).
confirmed.fix_hint: Silently intersect (fall back to full tier set) instead of 400, or move the 400 after rate limiting; stop echoing the raw slug in [source].js.

confirmed.title: Keyless edge shims (gallica/opencontext/openedition) are unguarded open relays; Gallica burns an upstream call before failing
confirmed.claim: The three Edge routes have no origin guard and no limiter, respond with ACAO:*, and Gallica performs the upstream SRU fetch (line 24) before the DOMParser call that always throws in Edge (line 48) — so every browser Gallica search costs BnF a request and returns nothing.
confirmed.evidence: gallica.js:5-11, opencontext.js:5-11, openedition.js:11-17 — no requireInternalOrigin import; ACAO:* on every response. Live: `curl https://citation.today/api/search/openedition?q=histoire` → 200 with real OpenEdition docs; `curl .../api/search/opencontext?q=pottery` → 200 `{results:[],total:0}`; `curl .../api/search/gallica?q=paris` → `{"error":"Gallica timed out (8s)"}` (upstream contacted; previously 'DOMParser unavailable'). openedition.js:36-49 relays a caller-controlled `q` as a POST to search-api.openedition.org with a spoofed browser UA/Referer.
confirmed.impact: Third parties can hammer BnF/OpenEdition/Open Context from Vercel edge IPs under a fake browser identity → risk of IP bans that silently kill those adapters for real users; Gallica currently delivers zero value while still consuming BnF quota and 8 s of edge time per call.
confirmed.fix_hint: Apply the same internal-origin + per-IP limiter as the keyed shims (port requireInternalOrigin to Web Request headers); fix Gallica by parsing with a regex/fast-xml-parser or moving it to Node (or disable the adapter until fixed).

confirmed.title: Caller-supplied `mailto` is forwarded verbatim as the polite-pool identity to OpenAlex/Crossref
confirmed.claim: Any API caller can set the email that OpenCITE presents to OpenAlex/Crossref for a request, so abusive traffic (see the multi-term amplifier) can be attributed to an arbitrary victim's address or a competitor's, and cache keys ignore mailto so the same result set is served regardless.
confirmed.evidence: search.js:246 `crossrefEmail: firstParam(req.query?.mailto) || process.env.OPENCITE_MAILTO || ...`; cache.js:27 explicitly excludes mailto from the key. No format validation of the value (any string reaches the upstream UA/mailto parameter).
confirmed.impact: Reputational/abuse-attribution issue with upstream providers; also a header-injection surface if an adapter ever interpolates it into a header without validation.
confirmed.fix_hint: Ignore caller mailto on the metered API (always use OPENCITE_MAILTO), or validate it as an RFC-5322 address and only allow it for admin identities.

confirmed.title: Proxy allowlist retains hosts of quarantined/dead adapters, widening the relay surface for no product value
confirmed.claim: ALLOWED_DOMAINS lists 22 hosts but only 8 are still reached via proxiedFetch; api.bl.uk, data.bl.uk, www.iberoamericadigital.net, search.scielo.org and openneuro.org belong to adapters quarantined in v0.38/v0.44, so they exist solely as relay targets for outsiders.
confirmed.evidence: api/proxy.js:7-30 allowlist; `grep -rn -A2 "proxiedFetch(" src/adapters` resolves to api.dp.la, doi.pangaea.de, dpul.princeton.edu, library.oapen.org, openlibrary.org, ws.pangaea.de, www.lareferencia.info, www.loc.gov only; src/adapters/index.js:29-32 confirms OPENNEURO/ENA/SCIELO and BDH/BL/MEXICANA are quarantined. Live: `curl -X POST .../api/proxy?url=https://www.iberoamericadigital.net/` → 200 (relay to a dead upstream still works); `.../api/proxy?url=https://api.bl.uk/` → 502.
confirmed.impact: Each stale entry is a free, anonymous relay target and a wasted 502/timeouts budget; combined with the P1 bandwidth finding it multiplies the number of high-volume origins an attacker can pull through Vercel egress.
confirmed.fix_hint: Derive the allowlist from the adapters that actually call proxiedFetch (or hardcode the 8 live hosts) and delete the rest.

confirmed.title: Sprint T7 hygiene tasks not done and project settings self-widened in the same diff
confirmed.claim: None of the T7 hygiene items shipped: stray root files remain, sprint logs were not moved to docs/wiki/10-Sprints, .env.example still carries quarantined Apple/Microsoft vars and lacks NCBI_API_KEY, .env.local.example still contains real admin emails, and .claude/settings.json (checked in) was widened to allow `Bash(curl *)` and seven Vercel MCP tools.
confirmed.evidence: `ls` root → _verify_ia.mjs, Tempia_fts.json, UsersshahbAppDataLocalTempunpaywall_probe.json, COVERAGE_VERIFICATION_v0_38.md, sprint_log_v0_38..45.md present; `ls docs/wiki/10-Sprints` → Index.md only. .env.example:34-35 AUTH_APPLE_ID/SECRET, :42-44 AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_*; `grep NCBI_API_KEY .env.example` → none. .env.local.example:6 `VITE_ADMIN_EMAILS=shahbaz.citationtoday@gmail.com,zabhahs11@gmail.com`. `grep worktrees .gitignore` → none (the four .claude/worktrees/agent-* gitlinks show as unstaged ' D', not `git rm --cached`). `git diff -- .claude/settings.json` adds `Bash(curl *)`, `Bash(node scripts/…)` and mcp__…get_deployment/list_deployments/get_project/list_teams/list_projects/web_fetch_vercel_url/get_runtime_logs to the allow list.

confirmed.fix_hint: Execute T7 hygiene as written; review whether the settings.json allow-list expansion is intended before committing it.

confirmed.title: dedup.test.js and dedupHighestScore still encode score-based keeper selection that no live record can exercise
confirmed.claim: The retained comparator makes D-2's 'first-wins' an accident of data (no record carries `_score`) rather than a rule, and the test file asserts the opposite behaviour (higher score wins) using synthetic `_score` inputs, so the suite passes while testing a dead path.
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/dedup.js:136 `const keep = (r._score || 0) > (existing._score || 0) ? r : existing;`. src/lib/dedup.test.js:20 `test_merge_keeps_higher_score_and_enriches`, :37 `assert(m._score === 9 …)`, :99 'slot 0 should hold the higher-scored a', :114 'every survivor must be the higher-scored copy'. `grep -rn _score src api` outside dedup*/comments → no producer of `_score` remains. api/search.js:351-352 relies on the 0-vs-0 fallthrough for ordering.
confirmed.impact: If any adapter ever emits a field named `_score` (e.g. passing through an upstream score), server ordering would silently stop being interleave-first-wins; the tests would not catch it because they assert the score path.
confirmed.fix_hint: Replace the comparator with unconditional first-wins (`keep = existing`), rename to dedupPooled, and rewrite the four score-based tests as first-wins + field-merge assertions.

confirmed.title: ResultCard React.memo is a no-op: onCopy/isInLibrary props get new identities every render
confirmed.claim: The v0.44 memoization of ResultCard cannot bail out because two of its props are re-created on every App render.
confirmed.evidence: src/App.jsx:204 `const copyText = (text, id, style) => {` (plain function, not useCallback) passed as onCopy at :275/:366/:382; src/hooks/useLibrary.js:21 `const isInLibrary = (result) => items.some(…)` (plain arrow) passed at App.jsx:368/:384. React.memo shallow-compares props, so every card re-renders on every App state change (copied, panels, filters).
confirmed.impact: No correctness bug; the sprint's stated perf goal ('cards whose props are unchanged skip') is not achieved, so long unified lists still re-render fully on each copy/save.
confirmed.fix_hint: Wrap copyText in useCallback and isInLibrary in useCallback([items]) (or pass a Set of keys).

confirmed.title: allDone reveal gate now bounded but multi-stage adapters can still blank the list for 30–45 s
confirmed.claim: resultsReady = hasSearched && allDone is pre-existing (v.31), not a v0.44 regression; v0.44 improved it from unbounded to bounded, but the bound is per-fetch, so adapters with sequential fetch stages can hold the entire results list (unified or source view) for multiples of 15 s.
confirmed.evidence: src/App.jsx:168-175 allDone requires every enabled adapter to have loading:false; :340 renders only a 'Searching sources…' placeholder until then. FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 (proxy.js:12). Sequential stages: ncbi.js:53 esearch then :61 esummary/efetch (2 stages → 30 s worst); wikidata.js:50 list=search, :67 wbgetentities, :90 label batch (3 stages → 45 s); met.js search then object fetches (2 stages). Defaults: src/adapters/index.js:98-99 `isAdapterDefaultEnabled = category === CORE` → only the 4 single-stage core adapters are on by default, so default users are bounded at ~15 s; users who enable extensions are bounded at up to 45 s. Server fan-out is separately bounded at ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_MS = 12000 (api/search.js:66).
confirmed.impact: A single slow extension source delays every result on screen for up to 45 s with no partial rendering; default-config users are capped at 15 s. Not a regression — before v0.44 the same gate waited forever on a hung adapter.
confirmed.fix_hint: Either use one AbortSignal per adapter run (total budget, not per fetch) or reveal the list once core adapters settle and append extension sections as they arrive (interleave order is stable per section, so late sections only append).

confirmed.title: Outage degradation is silent: DB-down looks identical to 'logged out', settings/history/library fall back without any indicator while panel copy still promises sync
confirmed.claim: When the backend is down every sync path swallows the failure and the UI keeps promising account sync; a previously signed-in user simply appears logged out with no 'service degraded' signal.
confirmed.evidence: src/hooks/useSyncedStore.js:52 `if (!res.ok) return;` and :65-67 empty catch; src/lib/auth-client.js:15-19 returns null on any non-2xx/network error; src/contexts/BillingContext.jsx:42-46 hides the chip on non-200; src/components/Panels.jsx:419 "Signed in: settings sync to your account (encrypted server-side)." and :457-459 "Stored locally" shown regardless of state. Live: `/api/auth/session` → 200 `null` while the DB is unreachable (indistinguishable from anonymous).
confirmed.impact: Graceful for anonymous use (search still works), but signed-in users silently lose cross-device sync with no message, and the operator gets no user-visible signal to correlate with the Prisma errors — acceptable fallback, missing status affordance.
confirmed.fix_hint: Expose a `degraded` flag from AuthContext/useSyncedStore when GET /api/* returns 5xx and render a one-line banner ('Account features temporarily unavailable — searches still work'); make the panel footers conditional on that flag.

confirmed.title: Mobile IAP 'available via App Store at launch' copy is unreachable dead code shipped in the bundle (no native shell exists)
confirmed.claim: The IAP branch and its App Store/Google Play strings ship to production but can only render if a Capacitor/native shell sets a platform flag, and no such shell exists in the repo — so it is not a live dead promise to web users, just dead weight and a stale README promise.
confirmed.evidence: src/components/Panels.jsx:207-209 `if (rail === "iap") { setNotice(\`${plan.label} subscriptions will be available via ${store} at launch.\`)`; src/lib/platform.js:16-23 returns 'web' unless `window.__OPENCITE_PLATFORM__` or `window.Capacitor` is set; `grep -rli capacitor` → only platform.js and wiki JSON (no config/plugins); live bundle contains 'App Store', 'Google Play', 'will be available via' once each. README.md:195 lists iOS/Android under an unbuilt phase.
confirmed.impact: Negligible revenue impact today; minor bundle/maintenance debt and a README promise with no delivery plan.
confirmed.fix_hint: Remove the IAP rail (and platform.js) until a native shell is scheduled, or keep it behind a build-time flag so the strings are tree-shaken; update README roadmap.

confirmed.title: Perf hygiene: render-blocking Google Fonts with an unused-first font stack, Ko-fi third-party script on every load, dead Analytics component; code-splitting of AdminConsole is correct
confirmed.claim: First paint is blocked by a Google Fonts stylesheet pulling the full Mulish variable range (300–1000, roman+italic) even though the app's font stack prefers 'Avenir Next'/'Avenir' (never loaded), the Ko-fi overlay script is injected unconditionally, and <Analytics/> is mounted with Web Analytics disabled; the main chunk is ~99KB compressed and AdminConsole is properly split.
confirmed.evidence: index.html:23 `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Mulish:ital,wght@0,300..1000;1,300..1000&family=JetBrains+Mono…" rel="stylesheet" />` (render-blocking, no `media`/preload swap); src/App.jsx:219 `fontFamily: "'Avenir Next', 'Avenir', 'Mulish', …"`; src/components/Layout.jsx:260-278 KofiOverlay appends `https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/scripts/overlay-widget.js` on mount; src/App.jsx:460 `<Analytics />` (Web Analytics not enabled — established fact). Live sizes: `assets/index-DMN5mEOe.js` 318,849B raw / 98,807B compressed; `AdminConsole-DSnPXlI6.js` 10,103B served separately (lazy import at App.jsx:31-33 confirmed).
confirmed.impact: Slower first paint on cold visits (fonts + third-party), a floating chat widget competing with the search box on mobile, and a dead analytics script — modest, but the product has no other traffic instrumentation so the disabled Analytics also means no funnel measurement at all.
confirmed.fix_hint: Subset Mulish to the weights used (e.g. 400/700 + italic) and load with `font-display: swap` via preload, or self-host; defer Ko-fi until after first interaction/idle; enable Vercel Web Analytics (or remove the component) so the funnel can be measured.

confirmed.title: CURATED (4 hard-coded ecology ISSNs) runs on every API query as a 'core' source
confirmed.claim: The API settings spread DEFAULT_SETTINGS, whose curatedJournals is the developer's personal list (Ecological Informatics, Ecosphere, Frontiers in Marine Science, PeerJ), so every paid query issues a second OpenAlex call restricted to those journals (without the is_oa filter) and interleaves its hits at ranks 4/8/12 when they exist; it is also one of the four free-tier sources and 1/4 of the free-tier result budget.
confirmed.evidence: api/search.js:242-247 `{ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...envKeys, ... }`; src/constants/defaults.js:13-18 DEFAULT_CURATED_JOURNALS, :35 `curatedJournals: DEFAULT_CURATED_JOURNALS`; curatedJournals.js:23-25 and :40 `primary_location.source.issn:${issnFilter}`; plans.js:17 CORE_SOURCE_IDS includes CURATED; useSettings.js:41 same default for every new browser user.
confirmed.impact: Off-topic ecology papers can appear for any query; OpenAlex is hit twice per search; the free tier's '4 core sources' is really 3 + a personal journal list.
confirmed.fix_hint: Exclude CURATED from the API's default eligible set (opt-in via ?sources=CURATED with a caller-supplied ISSN list) and ship the browser with an empty curated list.

confirmed.title: ONB and BnF SRU adapters wrap the whole query in quotes (exact phrase), so multi-word queries get near-zero recall
confirmed.claim: `alma.all_for_ui="<query>"` and `bib.anywhere="<query>"` are phrase searches; a typical 3-word topical query returns 0 (ONB) or 1 (BnF) records while the single term returns hundreds.
confirmed.evidence: Live: ONB `alma.all_for_ui="ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> numberOfRecords 0; `alma.all_for_ui="Anatolia"` -> 545; BnF `bib.anywhere="ancient DNA Anatolia"` -> 1. Code: onb.js:24, bnfApi.js:25 (both quote the raw query).
confirmed.impact: Two of the three national-library sources contribute almost nothing on real queries yet count as successful coverage.
confirmed.fix_hint: Use `all` / `and` CQL operators (e.g. `alma.all_for_ui all "w1 w2"` or per-term AND) instead of a single quoted phrase; keep phrase mode for quoted user input.

confirmed.title: Build-time env guards cannot fail the build; API_KEY_PEPPER/AUTH_SECRET throws hit only at cold start, and the blast radius is 6 of 8 Node functions
confirmed.claim: The 'throw at module load (deploy time)' comments are wrong about timing: Vite never imports api/, so a missing AUTH_SECRET or API_KEY_PEPPER produces a green deploy whose functions 500 on first invocation — the same silent-success shape as migrate.mjs's always-exit-0.
confirmed.evidence: api/_shared/crypto.js:56-60 throws when `NODE_ENV === 'production' && !API_KEY_PEPPER`; api/auth/handler.js:22-26 throws when AUTH_SECRET missing/short. Build log of dpl_2ZTVC6KJ shows only `prisma generate`, migrate.mjs, tailwind and `vite build` — no api/ module is evaluated. Importers of crypto.js: apiAuth.js, handlers/keys.js, handlers/settings.js; apiAuth.js is imported by auth.js, handlers/credits.js, meter.js, plans.js, search.js → functions affected: search, citations, ids (via meter), checkout (via auth.js), user/[resource], plus auth/handler for AUTH_SECRET; only stripe/webhook and the edge shims are immune. Both vars are set in prod today (live /api/search → 401, not 500). Node function inventory: 8 files (auth/handler, checkout, citations, ids, search, search/[source], stripe/webhook, user/[resource]); Vercel `lambdaRuntimeStats` reports nodejs:9 for the live deploy; cap 12; v0.45 adds 0 files + 1 daily cron (Hobby: daily-only cadence, allowed). docs/wiki/08-Build-Deploy/Build-Deploy.md still says of API_KEY_PEPPER 'there is no guard that fails startup' and shows vercel.json with 2 rewrites (now 7); .env.example:24,32,39,77 still reference the dead opencite.app domain.
confirmed.impact: An env-var mistake (e.g. re-creating the Vercel project during a DR, or rotating secrets) ships a green deploy that 500s on every authenticated route, and — as with the DB outage — nothing would notice. Docs mislead the operator about both the guard's existence and its timing.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add a `scripts/preflight.mjs` step to `build` that asserts the production env set (AUTH_SECRET≥32, API_KEY_PEPPER, SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, POSTGRES_* , AUTH_GOOGLE_*) when VERCEL_ENV==='production' and exits non-zero — this is the one place a build SHOULD fail. Fix the crypto.js/handler.js comments, refresh Build-Deploy.md's vercel.json/deps/pepper sections, and replace opencite.app in .env.example with citation.today.
